title: fix(app): probe reads its picks in the setup frame in a turned setup
body:
## What changed

The Probe op read the picked feature's placement from the model
(`model::transform_of`). Generation judges the stylus against the facets
of the setup frame. In a setup that holds the part turned, the two reads
disagreed: the posted cycle sought a surface 10 mm inside the part, with
no refusal and no diagnostic.

- `operation::probe_pick`: the pick's placement now comes from
  `setup_align::pose_in(world, entity, setup)`. `probe_seed`,
  `probe_from_picks` and `probe_account` take `setup: Option<&str>`, the
  shape #2276 gave the Slot helpers.
- The call sites pass the operation's setup name:
  `commands::operation::geometry` (`SetOperationGeometry`),
  `operation::picks` and `operation::selection_memo`. Both of the last
  two already had it.
- `setup_align`: `OpParams::Probe` joins the verified mill kinds
  (`verified_mill`), so Probe generates on `Mill` and `MillTurn` in an
  aligned setup. The refusal message now names Probe. Probe is not a
  turning kind: `verified_turn` is unchanged, and the lathe-post refusal
  in `lathe_voice` stays.
- Five sentinels pinned Probe as the refused kind. They now name kinds
  that are still unverified: a hand-carried `WireContour` params read
  through `generation_problem` (in the 2D-kinds, multi-axis and
  op-frame suites), a tilted Contour (the tilted-plane branch in
  `setup_align`), and the mill-turn loop. The mill-turn suite now
  asserts Probe is admitted there.

## Readings

- The generation arm already passed setup-frame facets to
  `probe_op::generate_probe` (the #2210 work). Only the seed read the
  model frame, so no other generation path needed a change.
- Probe's `KindInfo` is in `Section::Drilling`, so its family is Mill.
  One allowlist entry therefore covers `Mill` and `MillTurn`.
- The overtravel point is not a move: `probing::probe_cycle` records it
  in `path.probes` only. The moves stop at the tangent point, which is
  why a seeded touch stays clean while a stale target does not.
- The stylus law convicts a stale model-frame target because the feed
  from the safe plane crosses the turned part's top face on the way
  down.

## Pinning tests

- `setup_align_probe_kinds::turned_probe_reads_its_pick_in_the_setup_frame`
- `setup_align_probe_kinds::a_model_frame_target_in_a_turned_setup_is_convicted`

Negative control: with the old `model::transform_of` read, the first
test fails on the seed (`the turned seed: [20.0, 15.0, 10.0]`) and the
stylus law convicts that path (`Gouge` at moves 3 to 6). With the fix,
both tests pass.

## Not exercised

- No UI change: Probe was refused at generation only, so no ribbon or
  panel entry was blocked before, and none is blocked now.
- No MCP change: `set_operation_geometry` calls the same command, so it
  takes the setup-frame seed with this fix.
- A pick on a bore, boss, edge or vertex in a turned setup: every mode
  shares the one placement read that the face proof covers.
- The `Lathe` and `MillTurn` turning paths, and posts other than the
  built-in mill post.

## Notes

- The quick gate on this branch has five red binaries unrelated to the
  change, red at the branch point as well: `example_catalog`,
  `first_part_programs` and `wire_taper_angle` fail on CRLF checkouts of
  fixtures and goldens (#2523); `thread_boss` and `thread_mill` fail on
  stale NC goldens (tool numbers only). Checked: both stay red with the
  clean `origin/main` code in this same checkout.
- `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs` is already past the 400-line guide on
  `main` (457 lines). This change adds one line to it.
- `SetOperationGeometry::new` and the job-collect region also carry
  changes in the open PRs #2149 and #2134. A conflict at merge time is
  expected; this branch takes `origin/main` only at merge time.

Changelog: Probe now generates in a setup that holds the part turned
(part alignment): its pick seeds the touch on the part as the setup
holds it, instead of a refusal (#2285).

Fixes #2285

title: feat(model): a linked model is imported again when its source file changes
body:
Stacked on #2542 (#2462): review the second commit, `feat(model): a linked model is imported again when its source file changes`. This PR goes back to `main` alone when #2542 merges.

## What changed

- **A model records its source file.** An import from a file records the path and the file's SHA-256 (`schema::ModelSource`, `crates/app/src/model_source.rs`). The record rides `ImportModel`, `UpdateModel` (traded with the facets; undo restores it; a repair keeps it), `DeleteEntity` and `ImportFixture`. A mesh handed in, a browser pick and a generated fixture mesh record none.
- **Project v68.** A model row may have `source: {path, sha256}` (`project/source_dto.rs`). A v67 file steps up unchanged and opens unlinked. A source on a row that is not a model, an empty path, a bad digest or an unknown key is a corrupt file. An older CamCraft refuses a v68 file by name (`unsupported project version 68`).
- **The check** (`crates/ui/src/model_link_watch.rs`). In the window, each linked file is checked about once a second; the frame timer comes back for it while a model is linked. A file is read again only when its size or time moved. A new digest imports the file again through `CommandKind::ImportFile`, and `finish_import` lands a linked file on its model by name. This is the existing re-import: one `UpdateModel`, one undo step, the operations go Stale. **Nothing regenerates or posts.**
- **An undo of that import stays.** The check does not import the same bytes again; only a new change imports.
- **A missing or unreadable file** keeps the model as it is and is said on the status line one time.
- **Unlink.** The Browser's model menu has "Unlink from <file>" (`CommandKind::UnlinkModel`, `SetModelSource`, one undo step). The MCP tool `set_model_link` links (to a path, its digest recorded now, no import) or unlinks (`null`). `get_job` shows `models[].source`.
- **SHA-256** is the kernel's FIPS 180-4 code, re-exported as `camcraft_geometry::solidcraft::sha256_hex` (native only). No new crate dependency.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2463-linked-model.md`.

## Readings

Live app, debug build, macOS: `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7921 bracket.stl` (a 40 x 20 x 10 box).

- Before: `get_job` gives `bracket`, bounds max (40, 20, 10), `source.sha256` `00ee0c922a5b…`.
- The file is written again as a 40 x 20 x 25 box. Seven seconds later: bounds max (40, 20, 25), `source.sha256` `0158db27604b…`. No refusal in the log.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/model_link.rs`:
- `an_import_from_a_file_links_the_model_to_that_file`
- `an_update_trades_the_link_and_undo_restores_it`
- `delete_and_undo_keep_the_link`
- `link_and_unlink_are_one_undo_step_each_and_refuse_by_name`
- `the_project_file_keeps_the_link_and_a_v67_file_opens_unlinked` (also: a v69 file is refused by name)
- `a_malformed_source_row_is_refused_as_corrupt`
- `the_mcp_tool_links_and_unlinks_and_get_job_shows_the_source`

`crates/ui/src/model_link_tests.rs`:
- `a_changed_file_is_imported_again_as_one_undo_step_and_its_operations_only_go_stale` (a generated Face operation goes Stale, no generation starts, undo restores it and stays)
- `a_missing_file_keeps_the_model_and_is_said_one_time`
- `unlink_stops_the_check_and_undo_links_again`

`cargo xtask gate quick`: 857 steps, 0 failed (ui lib suite: 1098 passed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux: not run. The check uses std file metadata only.
- A window that the operating system reports as occluded does not draw frames (existing behaviour), so the check waits until the window is shown.
- A file renamed or moved away reads as missing; link it again with `set_model_link`. There is no "Link to file…" item in the window yet.

## Why

Solidcraft proposes "Send to CamCraft" (tangency-labs/solidcraft#18936, Solidcraft RFC 0001 phases 1 and 3). Each save in Solidcraft writes the `.sc` file again; with this, CamCraft updates the part after each save.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`: the `set_model_link` row).
Changelog: A model imported from a file is linked to it: when the file changes, the model is imported again (one undo step; its operations go Stale). Unlink from the Browser's model menu (#2463).
Effort: high
Fork synced at v0.23.0 (branch from upstream main 1d3d93541).

Fixes #2463

body:
## What changed

This PR makes main green again. Post-merge run 44320796021 on 8643d9bb7 had 4 failed steps of 874.

1. `examples/first-router-part.nc` has new content, recorded from `camcraft-cli process examples/first-router-part.camproj`. One line changes: `G73 X53 Y50 Z-13 R0 Q4 F150` becomes `G73 X53 Y50 Z-14.803 R0 Q4 F150`.
2. `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc` has new content. Only the tool comment, `T` and `H` lines change: TM-0600-P125 T02/H02 -> T01/H01, TAP-DRILL T01/H01 -> T02/H02.
3. `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc` has new content. Only the tool comment, `T` and `H` lines change: TM-0600-P125 T02/H02 -> T01/H01, EM-1000-4FL T01/H01 -> T03/H03.
4. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_projects.rs`: the demo projects go to `<temp>/camcraft-guide-projects-<pid>`, and the test removes that directory at the end. `CAMCRAFT_GUIDE_PROJECTS_OUT` still selects the output for `cargo xtask docs-images` and the catalog media. A new test pins the default path.
5. `docs/decisions/2543-main-red-posts.md` records the decision.

## Cause of each failure

- `first_part_programs::first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`: #2504 (merge 90e016a6e) and #2488 (merge c9b1366ac) clash.
  - #2504 saved `examples/first-router-part.camproj` at v68 with `"break_through_from": "full_diameter"`.
  - #2488 recorded the `.nc` pin at the same time, so neither PR saw the change of the other.
  - The new depth is correct. The extra 1.803 mm is the point length of the 6 mm 118 deg drill: `3 / tan(59 deg) = 1.803`.
- `thread_mill::a_multi_form_mill_threads_m8_clean_and_posts_helical_moves` and `thread_boss::an_external_m8_thread_verifies_clean_and_posts_helical_moves`: #2488 (merge c9b1366ac) makes tool numbers stable.
  - `AddTool` gives the lowest free number in the order of addition.
  - The fixtures add the thread mill first, so the thread mill is now T01.
  - Each operation still calls its own tool with the matching `H` word. No motion line changes.
- `egui_app::tests::guide_projects::demo_projects_build_and_load_with_valid_paths`: the runner environment causes this failure. It is not a regression.
  - The gate log artifact shows `save /tmp/camcraft-guide-projects/guide-workholding.camproj: I/O error: Permission denied (os error 13)`.
  - A fixed name in a shared temp directory belongs to the first account that makes it.
  - The failure is older than this window: runs 44285991575, 44296963679 and 44302217388 also failed it. The test came from #1902.

No failure is wrong posted G-code. Thus no issue is P1.

## Pinning tests

- `first_part_programs::first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`
- `thread_mill::a_multi_form_mill_threads_m8_clean_and_posts_helical_moves`
- `thread_boss::an_external_m8_thread_verifies_clean_and_posts_helical_moves`
- `egui_app::tests::guide_projects::demo_projects_build_and_load_with_valid_paths`
- `egui_app::tests::guide_projects::default_projects_dir_belongs_to_this_process` (new)

## Gate results

- Each binary, run one by one: first_part_programs 2/2, thread_boss 12/12, thread_mill 8/8, guide_projects 3/3.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. The app crate has only golden changes.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on base 37bde5e9a: 555 steps, 0 failed, 53.4 min.

- The ui fix is not run on the Linux runner account that owns the old `/tmp/camcraft-guide-projects`. The next post-merge run shows it.
- Main moved to 7491ce4d6 after the gate. `git merge-tree` shows a clean merge. Only `crates/app/src/commands/operation/geometry.rs` changed in the touched area (2 lines). The gate did not run on the merged tree.

title: fix(ui): Tab, Shift+Tab and Enter move between the value fields of a page
body:
#2516: in a group of value fields, Enter did not move the focus to the next value field, and Tab seemed not to move it either.

## What I found

egui's own Tab moved the focus, but in draw order over each focusable widget. On the operation property panel, Tab from a value field went to:

- a group header (it has no visible focus mark), then
- a checkbox or a combo, then
- the action bar: Generate, Clear toolpath, Close and Delete operation.

Thus the focus seemed to leave the form. Enter committed the value and dropped the focus (egui's default for a DragValue).

## What changed

- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/layout/field_ring.rs`: a ring of the value fields of the Properties pane.
  - The form seam's number helpers in `fields.rs` register each field (`num`, `num_feed`, `num_narrow`, the `num_*_row`/`_named`/`_by` forms, `num_plain`, `int_range_row`, `num_unit`).
  - `group_open` (`layout/form.rs`) marks the group of the fields in its body.
  - `pages::properties` opens the ring before the pane and closes it after.
- From a registered field:
  - Tab moves to the next field, and Shift+Tab to the previous one. The ring wraps at the two ends.
  - Enter commits the value to the draft (as before) and moves to the next field of the same group. After the group's last field, the focus drops (as before).
  - From a combo, a checkbox or a button, egui's own order stays.
- The moved-to field gets the focus when the next frame begins, before any widget draws. Thus egui's DragValue selects its text, and a typed number replaces the old one, as after a click. A repaint is requested for that frame.
- Focus is ephemeral UI state and queues no command. A value still reaches the document only through Apply (`EditOperationParams`).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2516-field-focus.md`.

## Tests

- `egui_app::field_focus_tests` (new, on the real operation property panel of a Pocket op):
  - `tab_and_shift_tab_walk_the_value_fields_and_wrap` (Heights): Tab goes 25 → 12 → 9 → 1 → 25, past the combos and the group headers. Shift+Tab wraps from the first field to the last, then goes back. No command is queued.
  - `enter_commits_the_value_and_moves_to_the_next_field_of_its_group` (Feeds): a typed 750 lands in the draft, and the focus moves to the plunge feed. A typed 150 there replaces the old value. The document keeps 800 until Apply. Enter in the group's last field drops the focus.
- `egui_app::layout::field_ring::tests` (3): the pure rule (wrap, Enter within the group only, no move from a widget outside the ring).
- Mutation check: with the ring's move switched off, both panel tests fail.
- Changed: the `thread_hand_tests` helpers `edit_number` and `type_dip` click a field only when it is not focused. After Enter, the next field already has the focus with its text selected. A click on a focused field only places the cursor, so the typed text was appended.

Gates on 213874858:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 9 steps, 0 failed (`ui lib` and the 7 UI suites of the gate map). The last edit after the gate is a clippy fix (`Option::replace`), with the same behaviour. The `field_` and `thread_hand` tests (18) are green after it.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised

- No hand test in the real window. The tests drive the real `pages::properties` code through the harness.
- Fields drawn with a raw `DragValue` outside the form seam helpers are not in the ring. egui's own Tab order stays for them (#1122 moves the pages to the seam).
- Dialogs outside the Properties pane (for example the tool library window) are not in the ring.

Changelog: In the Properties pane, Tab and Shift+Tab move between the value fields, and Enter commits a value and moves to the next field of its group (#2516)

Effort: medium (the label of the issue). Not escalated.

Fixes #2516

title: feat(machine): a machine file names its post, and the Setup page offers it
body:
**What changed**

- A `.mch` file can state `controller.post`, the name of a built-in post. `Machine.post`
  holds it. A file without the key reads as before.
- The reader refuses a value that is not a non-empty string, at `controller.post`
  (`post::machine::post_name`).
- The validator also refuses a name that is not a built-in post, and a post that does not
  serve the machine's kind. The post crate gets the registry as a closure, as the holder
  lookup does (#828), so there is no new crate edge.
- `posting::post_offer` returns `Option<PostOffer>`. It offers the machine's named post
  (`OfferWhy::Machine`) when that post is in the registry, serves the mount, and is not
  the setup's post. Otherwise it gives the kind offer as before (`OfferWhy::Kind`). A
  `.cps` file post is never offered over.
- The Setup page's banner tells which offer it is: "the machine names grblHAL as its post;
  switch to it?" or the kind text as before. The button queues `SelectPostNamed`, so it
  rides undo.
- A mount never changes the post by itself (#343, #388).
- The MCP tools say the same, after the QA finding on #2374. `post_offer_for` asks for any
  setup (`posting_offer.rs`). `load_machine` replies with `post_offer` for the setup that it
  mounted to, and `get_job` gives `post_offer` for each setup: the post, why, and the
  `set_setup_post` call that takes it. `null` means no offer.
- The description of the `post` tool lists every name in `BUILTINS`. The hand-written list
  did not have "Tormach PathPilot", grblHAL, TinyG or the Carvera posts.
- 32 shipped machine files state their post, where `MACHINES`, a machine's issue or its
  post writes the pairing: the PathPilot mills, routers, lathes and plasma table, grblHAL
  and the Sienci AltMills, TinyG, the Makera machines, the Doosan DNM 5700s and the Haas
  machines. The generic machines, the Sodick ALC400G, the Mach3-era Tormach mills and the
  sinker template state none.
- The Machines pane's file editor gives a user's own machine its post. General has a Post
  row, a dropdown (`Field.choices`) of the built-in posts that serve the file's kind, plus
  "(none)", which takes the key out. A stated name off the list stays in view with its
  refusal. Only built-in posts are offered: a `.cps` file has no stable name for a machine
  file to state.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2374-machine-names-its-post.md`.

**Readings**

Branched from `main` at `6349a542e`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 346 steps, 0 failed, on `2d26ef2a3`.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --base upstream/main`: 837 steps, 836 ok, 61.9 min. The one red step was
  `clippy -D warnings` (`bool::then` with a closure in `posting_offer.rs`), fixed in
  `a9205467b`; that step reran green with `--failed`.
- After the editor's Post dropdown: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green,
  346 steps, 0 failed, 15.3 min, on the working tree committed unchanged as `b6bc94239`.
- By hand, the release build: a setup on the grblHAL machine is offered the grblHAL post
  and the switch rides undo; a user's own machine picks its post from the editor's dropdown,
  writes it, and the Setup page then offers it.

**Pinning tests**

- `crates/app/tests/machine_library.rs`:
  `a_machine_that_names_its_post_is_offered_it_and_the_choice_rides_undo`,
  `the_named_post_must_be_a_built_in_post_that_serves_the_machine`,
  `the_editor_offers_the_built_in_posts_that_serve_the_machine`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machine_named_post.rs`:
  `the_grblhal_machine_offers_its_own_post_and_the_switch_rides_undo`,
  `a_users_own_machine_picks_its_post_from_the_editors_dropdown`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_machine_post.rs`:
  `mounting_the_770mx_offers_pathpilot_and_the_agent_takes_it_as_one_undo_step`,
  `the_offer_follows_the_setup_the_machine_went_to_not_the_active_one`,
  `a_machine_that_names_no_post_and_serves_the_current_one_offers_nothing`,
  `the_post_tool_lists_every_registry_post`
- `crates/post/src/machine/post_name.rs`: five unit tests for the reader and the rule.
- Not changed and still green: the lathe-over-mill-post offer test in
  `ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`, `plasma_post.rs` (only moved to `offer.post`) and
  `sinker_burn.rs`.

**Not exercised**

- By hand: a `.cps` file post on the setup is not offered over. The tests pin it.
- An older reader on a new file. `Machine` is `#[serde(default)]`, so an older reader drops
  the key and loses only the offer, never a posted line. Thus no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump.
- The pairing for machines with no written pairing. They state no post, and the kind offer

title: feat(ui): open a model or project file given on the command line
body:
## What changed

`camcraft-ui <file>` opens one file at start:

- A model file (`.stl`, `.obj`, `.step`, `.stp`, and a Solidcraft `.sc` on native builds) is imported through `CommandKind::ImportFile`.
- A project file (`.camproj`) is opened through `CommandKind::OpenProjectFile`.

These are the commands of the Model and Project dialogs and of a drop. The worker, the update-or-spawn decision and the refusals stay shared (`crates/ui/src/launch_file.rs`).

The file arguments come from the same walk over the arguments as the option check (`cli_options::files`). An option's value (`--gpu nvidia`) is never read as a file. More than one file, an unknown extension, or a path that is not a file is refused by name on the status line (`open refused: ...`). The app then starts with an empty project. `--help` shows `Usage: camcraft-ui [options] [file]` and a `File:` section.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2462-open-file-argument.md`.

## Readings

- Live app, debug build, macOS: `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7915 testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc`. MCP `get_job` returns the model `solidcraft_for_beginners`, 279602 facets, bounds (-62.5, -62.5, 0) to (62.5, 62.5, 85), `can_undo: true`. The `.sc` import takes about 100 s in a debug build.
- Live app with `testdata/models/cube.stl`: `get_job` returns `cube`, 12 facets, bounds (0, 0, 0) to (1, 1, 1).

## Pinning tests (`crates/ui/src/launch_file_tests.rs`)

- `the_files_are_the_arguments_that_are_no_option_and_no_value`
- `help_shows_the_file_argument`
- `no_file_queues_nothing`
- `each_model_kind_is_imported_through_the_import_command` (STL, OBJ, STEP)
- `a_solidcraft_design_is_imported`
- `a_project_is_opened_through_the_open_command`
- `a_file_that_cannot_be_opened_is_refused_by_name`

`cargo xtask gate quick`: 9 steps, 0 failed (ui lib suite: 1095 passed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux: not run. The change has no platform code.
- macOS `open -a CamCraft part.sc`: macOS sends the file as an Apple Event, not as an argument. This change does not read Apple Events. To start the binary in the bundle with the path works.
- A running window that takes a file from a second start (single instance): out of scope (#2462).

## Why

Solidcraft proposes a "Send to CamCraft" command (tangency-labs/solidcraft#18936, Solidcraft RFC 0001 phase 1) that starts CamCraft with a design's path. The linked-model follow-up is #2463.

Changelog: `camcraft-ui <file>` opens a model or project file given on the command line (#2462).

Fork synced at v0.23.0 (branch from upstream main 1d3d93541).

title: fix(post): write P0 on zero-dwell G86 in grblHAL and Tormach
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/grblhal.cps` (`onCycle`) and `assets/posts/tormach.cps` (`onCycle`) now emit `"P" + secs(dwell)` whenever `g === "G86"`.
- A zero-dwell bore now writes `P0` on every opening `G86` block instead of omitting `P`.
- Modal `X Y` holes inside an open `grblhal.cps` group still omit `P`, while `tormach.cps` cancels with `G80` on each hop and writes `P0` on each new `G86` block.
- `G82` and `G89` still require `dwell > 0` for `P`, and zero-dwell `BACKBORE` still emits `G85` without `P`.
- Recorded the decision in `docs/decisions/2362-g86-zero-dwell.md` (branched from `upstream/main` `4cab68f97`).

## Cause

Both posts gated the cycle `P` word on `dwell > 0 && (g === "G82" || g === "G86" || g === "G89")`.
Because LinuxCNC's `convert_cycle_xy` requires a non-negative `P` word on the first `G86` block after `G80` or at cycle start, and grblHAL follows the LinuxCNC canned-cycle specification, zero-dwell `G86` blocks omitted `P`.

## Tests

- Pinning tests in `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs`: `grblhal_zero_dwell_g86_has_p0`, `tormach_zero_dwell_g86_has_p0`, and `canned_posts_write_g86_and_no_other_cycle` all failed before the fix and pass after it (all 9 tests in `bore_cycle` pass).
- Mutation checks:
  - Restored `upstream/main` `assets/posts/grblhal.cps` -> `grblhal_zero_dwell_g86_has_p0` failed; restored the fix -> passed.
  - Restored `upstream/main` `assets/posts/tormach.cps` -> `tormach_zero_dwell_g86_has_p0` failed; restored the fix -> passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 130 of 130 steps passed (90 `camcraft-post` steps and 40 `camcraft-app` steps, wall 3.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed with no warnings.

## Goldens moved

- `crates/post/tests/golden/bore/grblhal.nc`: line 15 changed `G86 X10 Y10 Z-12 R2 F120` to `G86 X10 Y10 Z-12 R2 P0 F120`.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/bore/tormach.nc`: lines 19 and 25 changed both `G86` blocks to include `P0`.

## Not exercised

- Physical grblHAL and Tormach PathPilot controller hardware were not run; behavior relies on the LinuxCNC G-code reference and grblHAL's public G-code list.
- Full `batch` and `release` gates were not run (only `quick` and `clippy`).

## Overlaps

- PR #2346 touches `assets/posts/tormach.cps` (`motionFor` lines already on `upstream/main` via #2386, not the `P`-word guard; touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes).
- PR #2506 touches `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (`EXPANDED` array only; touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes).
- PR #2515 touches `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (doc comment and `SECONDS` array only; touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes).

Effort: high
Changelog: grblHAL and Tormach posts write P0 on opening G86 bore cycle blocks when dwell is 0
Fixes #2362

title: fix(app): make main green again after #468/#2386, #2450 and #2488
body:
## What changed

The post-merge gate on main is red (runs 44279917425 and 44285991575). This PR fixes each cause. No assert is relaxed and no refusal is made wider. The reasons are in `docs/decisions/2483-main-red-fixtures.md`.

1. `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`
   - Cause: commit 8f99bcb4c (Refs #419, merged with #468) changed `arc_chords` in `crates/cl/src/cl/moves.rs`. When the two radii differ (`ra != rb`), the step also obeys a curvature bound. One turning arc of the test part has radii that differ in the last float digits. It now posts 8 chords, not 7. #2386 made the golden on a base before that commit.
   - Fix: one hunk of `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc` (old lines 1326-1332) takes the 8 new lines. The rest of the golden does not change, so no Windows last-digit rounding enters it.
   - The new chords stay inside the chord tolerance. The end points and the end A do not change. The exact float compare is filed as #2520 (P7).
2. `stock_source_holes::framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number`
   - Cause: #2450 (49c268ba7) added the #2435 wall law. With a 10-degree tilt, the ride plane at the stock top (Z20) crosses the top face along a line that is no edge. The law refuses that line by name. The refusal is correct: a cone on that line cuts a groove, not a chamfer.
   - Fix: the fixture rides at mid-wall (`MID = 10.0`, `crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes.rs` near line 252). The added part's top moves with it. The asserts do not change. The test reaches the live refusal that it pins again.

title: fix(drill): name each hole wider than the drill, without holding the post
body:
#2496: `detect_holes` on a Drill op took holes wider than the drill. `generate` and `verify` then passed with no warning, and `post` wrote the program. Each such hole is drilled at the drill diameter, so it comes out undersize. Nothing told the user.

The fix follows the triage on the issue: name each hole that the drill does not make at its size. A pilot drill stays possible, so the post is not held.

## What changed

- **The law** (new `crates/app/src/operation/drill_size.rs`): `undersize_holes` gives each Z hole wider than the Drill-kind tool by more than `DRILL_SIZE_TOL` (0.1 mm on the diameter).
  - It reads only cycles that drill to size: Auto, Drill, Peck and Ream. Spot, Tap, FloatingTap, Bore and BackBore size the hole another way.
  - It reads only the mill's Z holes, not the turret's radial list.
  - A NaN or infinite hole radius, or a bad tool diameter, names nothing and does not panic.
- **Detect holes** keeps each such hole and names it in the new `DetectedHoles::undersize` list. Example: `the 8.000 mm hole at (-50.000, 0.000) is wider than the 6.000 mm drill: it is drilled 6.000 mm (a pilot) - use a 8.000 mm drill, or follow with a Bore or a reamer`.
  - MCP `detect_holes` answers it as `undersize`, beside `skipped`.
  - The GUI status line shows it. The GUI's pending command field `skipped` is now `notes`, with the skipped and the undersize sentences.
- **Generate** adds a new advisory `Warning::DrillUndersize { at, hole_mm, drill_mm }` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`) for each such hole, at its first cutting move.
  - `blocks_post()` is false, as for `Scallop`, `ProbeSearch` and `SinkerFinishOrder`.
  - MCP finding kind: `drill_undersize`.
  - The UI warning list groups it on its own line (key 216). `warned_moves` frames its move.
- The MCP tool description of `detect_holes` names `undersize` and `drill_undersize`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2496-drill-undersize.md`.

## Readings

- The issue's reproduction (D6, D8 and D12 through holes, catalog `DR-0600`) on a synthetic plate:
  - `detect_holes`: `holes: 3`, `skipped: []`, and `undersize` names the D8 and the D12 holes.
  - `generate`: `ok`, with two `drill_undersize` findings, `blocks_post: false`.
  - `verify`: `ok: true`. `post` writes the program.
- A D5 hole under the D6 drill: `verify` gives `ok: false` with a blocking `gouge`. The hole-wall excuse is capped at the facet sagitta (`WALL_SAG`, 0.05 mm), so it does not hide that cut. This law does not name it.

## Tests

- `crates/app/tests/drill_undersize.rs` (new, MCP):
  - `holes_wider_than_the_drill_are_named_at_detect_and_on_the_path_and_the_post_writes`
  - `a_hole_at_the_drills_own_size_names_nothing`
  - `a_hole_narrower_than_the_drill_is_held_as_a_gouge_not_named_undersize`
- `app::operation::drill_size::tests` (4): the size band (D6.04 and D6.1 are the drill's size, D6.2 and D8 are not), the narrower hole, the cycles and tool kinds that the law does not read, and the bad numbers.
- `ui::detect_holes_note_tests::detect_holes_on_a_drill_op_keeps_a_wider_hole_and_names_it_undersize`: the GUI status line.
- Mutation check: with the generate hook removed, the first MCP test fails (`one warning per undersize hole: []`).

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (325 steps, 23 min) ran on the first version, with a 0.05 mm band. 319 steps were green. 6 failed:
  - `drilling_axial::an_axial_drill_runs_clean_on_the_lathe_and_posts_its_cycle`: from this change. Its "matched" fixture has a 4 mm drill in a 4.1 mm hole, and the 0.05 mm band named it. The band is now 0.1 mm (5b16ed7e4), and the suite is green. A wider band names fewer holes, so it cannot make the 319 green steps fail.
  - `example_catalog` (2 tests), `first_part_programs` (2 tests), `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`, `stock_source_holes::framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` and `wire_taper_angle::an_incomplete_dialect_and_a_four_axis_angle_cut_are_refused_by_name`: not from this change. They fail the same way, at the same lines, on a clean worktree of the same base (bd0400ebb) on this Windows machine. `example_catalog` compares an LF program with the committed file read back with CRLF.
- On 5b16ed7e4: `drill_size` (4), `drill_undersize` (3), `drilling_axial` (7) and the GUI `detect_holes` tests (4): green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: one error, at `crates/app/src/operation/heights.rs:128`. That is #2479 (Clippy 1.99), in a file that this PR does not change. With only that lint allowed (`-A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args`): clean.

## Not exercised

- The turret's radial holes (`cross`). The law does not read them.
- The real STEP file of the issue. The test uses a synthetic STL plate with the same hole sizes.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

Changelog: A Drill operation names each hole wider than its drill, at Detect holes and as a warning on the toolpath that does not hold the post (a pilot drill stays possible) (#2496)

Effort: high (the label of the issue). Not escalated.

Fixes #2496

title: feat(post): Mach3 Mill post for 3-axis mills
body:
## What changed

A post script for Mach3 Mill (3-axis).

- `assets/posts/mach3.cps` (new). Derived from our `grblhal.cps`. Mach3 differences:
  - Tool change: Z goes up, then `T<n> M6` on its own line, then `G43 H<n>`. Mach3 runs the user's M6Start / M6End macros at M6; the post cannot know what they do, so it lifts Z first.
  - Canned cycles G73, G81, G82, G83, G85, G86, G89 with G98. P on G82, G86 and G89. A G83 dwell is refused by name (G83 has no P word).
  - Option `dwellInMilliseconds` (off by default): P in milliseconds, for a Mach3 with "G04 Dwell param in ms" on in General Config. Off writes seconds.
  - G91.1 in the header, so arc centres never depend on Mach3's IJ-mode setting.
  - G41/G42 control compensation, G84 tapping and probing are refused by name.
- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`: the post "Mach3" after Mach4, and its embedded copy.
- No new machine. A Mach3 user picks an existing 3-axis machine, for example "VMC 3-axis".

## Readings

- `drill_peck.nc`: `T4 M6`, `G43 H4`, then `G98`, `G73 X20 Y10 Z-24 R0 Q18 F60`, `G80`.
- Header: `G21 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G49 G80`.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/post/tests/script_mach3.rs` (new): `post_suite!("mach3.cps")` with its recorded goldens.
- `mach3` added to the shared post tables: `conformance` (with refused cases and the synth stream), `post_spindle_rule_all`, `end_units`, `declared_options`, `comment_escape`, `comp`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `after_op`, `fanuc_post`, `bore_cycle` (`SECONDS`: G86 with P in seconds) and `dwell_cycles_modal_p` (P0.5 / P0.75).
- App goldens: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/mach3/*` and `synth_mach3.nc`, written with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick`: 623 steps, 1 failed. The failure is `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` (Tormach golden line count 3246 != 3245). This PR does not touch the Tormach post. It is the known red main in #2483.

## Not exercised

- No reading on a real Mach3 control and no air cut.
- That Mach3 accepts G91.1 and P on G86 is from the "Using Mach3Mill" word list only, not tested on a control.
- The `dwellInMilliseconds` option is checked in the goldens only with its default (off).

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2482-mach3-post.md`.

Changelog: New post "Mach3": T M6 + G43 H tool change, canned drill cycles with G98, dwell in seconds or milliseconds as a post option; G41/G42, tapping and probing refused.

title: fix(machine): remove unverified -360..360 A limit on microARC 4
body:
## What changed

Removed the invented `-360..360` `"travel"` field from `arc4` in `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`.
Added `general.description` citing Tormach mill operator manuals (`UM10587`, `UM10864`, `UM10349`), Tormach `TD10749`, and the PathPilot Hub readings (`v2.14.4`, 770MX SIM: `G1 A370`, `G93 A400`, continuous jog to `A 1484.663`).
Kept the cumulative A-travel refusal in `assets/posts/tormach.cps` active for any machine file that states a finite travel range.
Updated `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-4axis-part.md`, `site/tests/test_first_4axis_part.py`, and the Tormach rotary test suites to reflect unlimited A travel on PathPilot.
Added the decision record in `docs/decisions/2471-microarc4-unlimited-a-travel.md`.

## Cause

Issue #785 set A travel to `-360..360` because `TD10749` states no stops and indexing stayed within `-180..180`.
Tormach operator manuals (`UM10587`, `UM10864`, `UM10349`, Rotational Axis) specify that PathPilot treats A as a wrapped linear axis increasing or decreasing without limit toward +/- infinity.
LinuxCNC defaults unbounded angular limits to `-1e99..1e99`, and PathPilot Hub runs reached `A 1484.663` with no stop or alarm.
Under CamCraft's unstated-limit law (`assets/machines/AGENTS.md`), omitting `"travel"` states no travel limit (`None`), whereas `-360..360` made `assets/posts/tormach.cps` refuse legal multi-turn programs.

## Tests

New pins in `crates/post/tests/tormach_rotary_travel.rs`:
- `microarc_states_no_a_soft_limit_and_cites_sources`: asserts `a.travel == None` and source citations in `general.description`.
- `microarc_posts_multi_turn_rotary_offset_past_four_turns`: asserts +/-1500 deg Rotary Offset streams post cleanly on the shipped machine file.

New and updated pins in `crates/app/tests/tormach_wrapped_a.rs` and `crates/app/tests/tormach_fourth_axis.rs`:
- `shipped_microarc_posts_wrapped_a_past_four_turns`: asserts wrapped A posts cleanly through `A1500` on the shipped machine file.
- `the_microarc_machine_states_an_a_about_x`: asserts `a.travel == None` and `rotaries[0]["travel"] == null`.
- `a_count_past_the_travel_is_refused_by_name`, `positive_a_overtravel_names_the_rotary_offset_limit_and_remedy`, `negative_a_overtravel_names_the_rotary_offset_limit_and_remedy`, `rotary_offset_at_either_a_travel_boundary_still_posts`, and `an_a_past_travel_is_refused` confirm bounded machine files still refuse overtravel by name.

Mutation check: restoring `upstream/main`'s `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` failed `microarc_states_no_a_soft_limit_and_cites_sources`, `microarc_posts_multi_turn_rotary_offset_past_four_turns`, `shipped_microarc_posts_wrapped_a_past_four_turns`, and `the_microarc_machine_states_an_a_about_x`.
Restoring our fix passed all of them.

Checks run:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 8 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.
- App suites `first_4axis_part`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `index_swing`, `machine`, `machine_library`, `mcp_rotary_stack`, `rotary_subplate`, `rotary_subplate_standing`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, and `tormach_wrapped_a` passed; `microarc_test_part` failed on one pre-existing golden mismatch (`line count 3246 != 3245` on `wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`) that also failed identically against `upstream/main`'s unmodified machine file.
- `site/tests/test_first_4axis_part.py`: 12 passed, 1 pre-existing failure on `upstream/main` (`posting.rs` split into `posting_files.rs`, #2345); the updated machine travel assertion passed.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

Generated multi-turn Rotary Offset or >1500-degree wrapped programs were not run in PathPilot Hub or on hardware.
`zola check` and `crates/ui` suites were not run.

## Overlaps

PR #2346 touches `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-4axis-part.md` at a different line (intro cross-link vs machine-setup step here); whichever merges second refreshes.
PR #2346 also appears in GitHub file queries for `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`, `tormach_fourth_axis.rs`, `tormach_wrapped_a.rs`, and `test_first_4axis_part.py` from inherited commits of already-merged #2342, with no diff against `upstream/main` on those files.
Left `site/content/guide/multi-axis/_index.md` untouched because PR #2346 edits line 33 directly.

Changelog: Remove the unverified -360..360 A-travel limit from Tormach 770MX + microARC 4 so continuous multi-turn A programs post.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #2471

#2505: the kind check in `Tool::kind_rule` (`crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs`) ended with `_ => None`. A `ToolKind` added later passed the check with no kind rule. The equivalence test did not see it, because its kind list was written by hand.

A new `ToolKind` does not compile until this match names it.
- `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity_tests.rs`:
  - New `kind_slot`: an exhaustive match that gives each kind a slot. A new kind does not compile until it gets a slot.

title: feat(post): Grbl 1.1 post for 3-axis mills
body:
## What changed

A post script for Grbl 1.1 3-axis mills, and a machine for it.

- `assets/posts/grbl.cps` (new). Derived from our `grblhal.cps`. Grbl 1.1 has no canned cycles, no cutter radius compensation and no tool table, so:
  - Drill cycles post as G0/G1/G4 moves. The engine already sends the expanded hole moves, and the script passes them through (as `tinyg.cps` does). A dwell (P > 0) is a G4 at the hole bottom.
  - BORE and TAP are refused by name. An expanded bore needs a spindle stop before the rapid retract; a tap needs a synchronised spindle.
  - A tool change is a retract, a comment `(TOOL CHANGE - LOAD T<n> - SET Z ZERO - RESUME)` and `M0`. The first tool gets `(LOAD T<n> AND SET Z ZERO BEFORE THE START)`. No M6, no G43/G49.
  - G41/G42 control compensation is refused, as on TinyG.
  - A line is at most 79 characters (the Grbl 1.1 line buffer is 80 bytes with the terminator). A comment is cut to fit. A motion line that does not fit refuses the program.
- `assets/machines/grbl-3axis.mch` (new): a copy of `grblhal-3axis.mch`, model "Grbl 3-axis".
- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`: the post "Grbl 1.1" after TinyG, the machine "Grbl 3-axis", and their embedded copies.

## Readings

- `drill_peck.nc`: `(LOAD T4 AND SET Z ZERO BEFORE THE START)`, then G0/G1 pecks to Z-24 and a G0 retract. No G8x word.
- Longest line over all Grbl NC goldens: 43 characters.
- Refusal goldens (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/grbl/*.refusal`): rotary, C-axis live tool, probe and thread hand are refused by name.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/post/tests/script_grbl.rs` (new): `post_suite!("grbl.cps")` with its recorded goldens.
- `crates/post/tests/grbl_dialect.rs` (new): every line of every Grbl golden is at most 79 characters and has none of G73, G81-G89, G98, G99, G41, G42, G43, M6, O or H words.
- `grbl` added to the shared post tables: `conformance`, `post_spindle_rule_all`, `machine`, `first_traverse_clearance`, `end_units`, `declared_options`, `expanded_bore_refusal` (new test `grbl_refuses_expanded_bore`), post and app `bore_cycle`, `comment_escape`, `comp`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `program_units`, `after_op`, `fanuc_post`.
- `first_traverse_clearance.rs`: new helper `is_tool_change` reads M6 or the two Grbl tool comments as a tool change.
- App goldens: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/grbl/*` and `synth_grbl.nc`, written with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick` with the worktree's own target dir: 624 steps, 1 failed. The failure is `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` (Tormach golden line count 3246 != 3245). This PR does not touch the Tormach post. It is the known red main in #2483 (caused by #2386).

## Not exercised

- No reading on a real Grbl 1.1 control and no air cut.
- Grbl 1.1 receives G-code from a sender program. The sender's own limits are not checked.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2481-grbl-post.md`.

Changelog: New post "Grbl 1.1" and machine "Grbl 3-axis": drill cycles as plain moves, tool change as M0, bore, tap and G41/G42 refused, lines of 79 characters or less.

Fixes #2481

title: fix(drilling): include drill point length in through holes, stock sim, and MCP
body:
## Breaking project-format change

Saved projects now use v68, previously v67. Readers limited to v67 or earlier refuse v68 files instead of dropping `break_through_from` and changing drilling depths. This build migrates older files while preserving legacy `Tip` behavior. Commit `f1bbbee614d5ec580c60e173cb838af5b2288ff8` declares this incompatibility with `!` and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

## Levels controls before and after

These captures render the real egui shell with the same Drill Heights page and Levels controls. The viewport uses the test harness placeholder. The before capture uses the pre-feature Levels UI; the after capture shows the new `Break-through from` selector set to `Full diameter`. Images live only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Levels without the selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0920bf8e0d4387421b08d8b187fafab03366ea18/2504/before-levels.png) | ![After: Levels with Break-through from](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0920bf8e0d4387421b08d8b187fafab03366ea18/2504/after-levels.png) |

## Review-fix verification

Head: `f1bbbee614d5ec580c60e173cb838af5b2288ff8`.

- Selector pin `drill_break_through_from_defaults_to_full_diameter_and_switches_to_tip`: RED with the pre-feature selector removed, GREEN after restoration.
- Extended format pin `v65_preserves_cutting_steps_and_loads_v63_break_through_and_v62_defaults`: RED with the saved version changed to v67, GREEN after restoring v68. `wrong_version_is_refused` also passed.
- PR-body check: original body failed the screenshot-link check; updated remote body passed both immutable image links and the reader-limit check.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 589/592 steps passed in 35.6 minutes. The failures were the previously recorded `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` (3246 != 3245), `stock_source_holes::framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number`, and the review's `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds` (no graphics adapter). Both review-fix pins passed in this run.
- Strict Clippy for all targets of `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-app`, and `camcraft-ui` failed on the review's unchanged `crates/app/src/operation/heights.rs:128` warning. The same command passed with only `clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args` allowed.

## What changed

- Added `BreakThroughFrom` (`FullDiameter` by default, or `Tip`) to `Drill` parameters, UI (`Break-through from` combo in `holes_page.rs`), MCP DTOs, and project v68 (`PROJECT_VERSION = 68`).
- Added `drill_point_length` and `through_tip_run` in `camcraft_motion::drilling`. In `FullDiameter` mode on twist drills outside `Spot`, `Tap`, `FloatingTap`, and `Ream`, `through_tip_run` adds `(diameter / 2) / tan(tip_angle / 2)` (`180 deg -> 0.0`). Non-finite or out-of-range tip angles fail by name. Lathe axial drills keep `Tip` mode for `axial_doors` clearance.
- Migrated pre-v68 projects without `break_through_from` to `Tip` in `settle_drill_break_through`. Existing saved files keep their cached depths and posted Z.
- Added `SdfTool::Drill` and `RevKind::Drill` (`drill_dist`) in `camcraft_sim::stock_sim`, plus `simulate_drill` and `simulate_drill_display` across plain, display, carried, held, playback, field-view, and rest simulation.
- Listed `break_through` (`number`, default `null`) on `drill`, `bore`, and `thread` in `list_operation_types` (`crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`).

## Cause

Through holes with a twist drill added only `break_through` (`1.0 mm` default) to the tip depth, stopping the cylindrical margin ~0.803 mm short on a Ø6 118° drill. Both column and field stock simulation also modeled drills as flat cylinders at full diameter, hiding the uncut cone lip. Separately, `kind_defaults()` skipped `None` fields on serialization, so `list_operation_types` omitted `break_through`.

## Tests

### Pins (red before fix, green after)
- `issue_2441_through_hole_drill_adds_point_length_and_posts_full_breakthrough` (`crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`): failed before fix (`deepest tip must include the 118 deg drill point (-2.803), got -1.000`), passes after fix (posts `Z-19.803` and clears both sims at `r=2.5`).
- `issue_2441_stock_sim_models_drill_point_cone_lip_when_stopped_at_floor` (`crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`): failed before fix (`got z=0.000` flat bottom), passes after fix (leaves `~1.5 mm` cone lip at `r=2.5` in both sims when tip stops at `z=0`).
- `issue_2441_mcp_list_operation_types_lists_break_through` (`crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`): failed before fix (`drill is missing break_through`), passes after fix for `drill`, `bore`, `thread`, and `break_through_from`.
- `issue_2441_mcp_can_patch_break_through_and_break_through_from`, `drill_point_length_respects_tip_angle_and_refuses_bad_angles`, `through_exit_clears_the_floor`, `drill_engines_cut_cone_with_cylindrical_flute_and_agree`, `drill_break_through_from_defaults_to_full_diameter_and_switches_to_tip`: all pass.

### Mutation checks
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs` (`through_tip_run` reverted to `p.through_clear`): `issue_2441_through_hole_drill_adds_point_length_and_posts_full_breakthrough` failed RED -> restored GREEN.
- `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` (`ToolKind::Drill` cone & `drill` flag reverted to `(None, false)`): `issue_2441_stock_sim_models_drill_point_cone_lip_when_stopped_at_floor` failed RED -> restored GREEN.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs` (`break_through` injection removed in `list_operation_types`): `issue_2441_mcp_list_operation_types_lists_break_through` failed RED -> restored GREEN.
- `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs` (`settle_drill_break_through` skipped for `from < 68`): `v65_preserves_cutting_steps_and_loads_v63_break_through_and_v62_defaults` failed RED -> restored GREEN.

### Gate and Clippy
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (`exit 0`).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (at `5485b6476`): 589/592 steps passed in 78.2 minutes. All `sim` (41/41), `motion` (5/5), and `ui` (9/9) steps passed. Three `camcraft-app` suites reported failures:
  - `shoulder_adaptive` (`containment_outside_clears_past_the_edge_never_the_recess` hit its 60 s debug timer under 6-way contention, tracked by #2453): re-running `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test shoulder_adaptive -- --test-threads=1` passed 9/9 (69.42s).
  - `microarc_test_part` (`a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`, `3246 != 3245` lines): pre-existing failure on `upstream/main` tracked by #2483 and reproduced in `upstream/main` post-merge CI run `44279917425`.
  - `stock_source_holes` (`framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number`): pre-existing failure on `upstream/main` since `7bcc13a4b` and reproduced in `upstream/main` post-merge CI run `44279917425`.
- Targeted suites observed inside the `5485b6476` gate run: `break_through` (12/12), `operations` (120/120, 6 ignored), `first_router_part` (4/4), `example_catalog` (2/2), `mcp` (22/22), `golden_cl` (33/33), `solid_law_goldens` (7/7).

## Goldens moved

- No `.cl` goldens changed (`git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.cl"` is empty).
- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc` (plus `first-part.camproj` and `README.md`): only the four `Drill1` (`DR-0600`) cycles moved (`G73 X... Y... Z-1. R22. Q18. F300` -> `G83 X... Y... Z-2.803 R22. Q6. F300`), as adding the `1.803 mm` point crosses the `4d` (`24 mm`) `Auto` depth threshold into `G83`.
- `examples/first-router-part.camproj` (plus `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-router-part.md`): regenerated `Drill1` moves and cycle `bottom_z` from `-1.0` to `-2.802582` (`G73 ... Z-14.803` in `G54`); `2D Pocket1` and `2D Contour1` paths are unchanged.

## Not exercised

- Interactive GPU viewport rendering was not run; field and column drill cones were checked numerically in unit tests and `stock_view::field_view`.
- Radial cross drilling (`cross_drill`) keeps its own existing through math and does not read `break_through_from`.
- The full `release` tier (with `--ignored` heavy lanes and Windows UI pixel snapshots) was not run.

## Overlaps

Touches the same file (different functions/arms or regenerated assets; whichever merges second refreshes):
- #2503 (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` 2D extension / keep-law arm)
- #2488 (`crates/app/src/project/apply.rs` `freeze_legacy_tool_numbers`, `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` `ToolDto`)
- #2486 (`examples/first-router-part.camproj`)
- #2460 (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` 2D Contour arms)
- #2253 (`crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, `generate.rs`, `project/file.rs` `PROJECT_VERSION`, `project/apply.rs`, `crates/app/tests/units_in_refusals.rs`; already has `conflicts`)
- #2149 (`crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, `generate.rs`, `project/file.rs`, `project/apply.rs`; already has `conflicts`)
- #2134 (`crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, `project/file.rs`, `project/apply.rs`, `crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`; already has `conflicts`)
- #2092 (`crates/app/src/project/file.rs`, `project/apply.rs`, `crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`)
- #2024 (`crates/app/src/project/apply.rs`)
- #1713 (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` Finish3D arms, `kinds.rs`, `project/params.rs`, `project/params_impl.rs`, `crates/app/tests/golden_cl.rs`, `crates/app/tests/operations.rs`, `crates/motion/tests/center_cut_owed.rs`)

Changelog: Include drill point length in through-hole break-through by default (`Full diameter` vs `Tip`), simulate twist-drill cones accurately, and expose `break_through` in MCP `list_operation_types`.

Fixes #2441

title: fix(2d): keep extension out of islands and note uncut corners
body:
## What changed

- Populated `AreaCtx::blocked` in `crates/app/src/operation/boundary_ctx.rs` for whole-model (`SrcRef::Entity`) and stock-source (`SrcRef::Stock`) pocket-family operations (`2D Pocket`, `2D Adaptive`, `2D Offset`) while keeping `islands` as `false`.
- Added `unreached_corners` and `unreached_corner_note` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs` (re-exported in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`) to detect residual sharp-corner cusps wider than `0.03 mm` half-width and clip them against the setup stock outline so extended air corners do not warn.
- Updated `keep_law::narrow_noted` and its call site in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` to append the corner residual note on clearing operations around parts.
- Surfaced non-empty operation `path.notes` as `"notes"` in `crates/app/src/script/api.rs::op_view` so MCP `generate` and `verify` report the corner note without changing empty responses.
- Updated `crates/app/tests/keep_law.rs` (`a_whole_model_extension_keeps_the_part_and_posts`), added `crates/app/tests/adaptive_zero_margin_island.rs`, and recorded the choices in `docs/decisions/2438-adaptive-zero-margin-corners.md`.

## Cause

Default whole-model and stock-source clearing keeps the cutter inside the setup stock box, which necessarily leaves uncut triangular corner cusps at sharp 90-degree stock corners around an island. The narrow-band detector only reported whole disconnected bands that eroded to empty, and `op_view` did not expose `path.notes`, so callers saw an `ok` verdict with silent unreached stock corners. Meanwhile, `boundary_ctx::build` left `blocked = None` for `SrcRef::Entity` and `SrcRef::Stock` pocket-family operations, so setting `Boundary` `extension` to clear the stock corners shrank the interior island hole too and drove cuts straight through standing part geometry.

## Tests

- **Pins (`crates/app/tests/adaptive_zero_margin_island.rs`)**:
  - `zero_margin_adaptive_around_island_names_uncut_stock_corners`: failed on unchanged `7bcc13a4b` (missing `notes` in MCP `generate`), passes after fix (verifies `rest.max > 4.0` and corner note on `generate` and `verify`).
  - `extension_on_island_on_plate_grows_only_exterior_clears_corners_part_source` and `_stock_source`: failed on unchanged `7bcc13a4b` (`verify` reported island gouges), pass after fix (zero gouge cells, stock corners cleared to floor, posts cleanly, no corner note).
  - `extension_with_top_allowance_keeps_island_untouched_and_clears_corners`: failed on unchanged `7bcc13a4b` (`Gouge` + `RapidInStock`), passes after fix under `+2 mm` stock allowance.
- **Unit tests (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs::law`)**: 4 tests pass (`sharp_stock_corners_around_island_are_named_until_extended`, `filleted_corners_and_unreached_bands_emit_no_corner_note`, `a_band_narrower_than_the_tool_beside_a_wide_bore_is_named`, `a_noise_sliver_and_an_empty_region_say_nothing`).
- **Keep law (`crates/app/tests/keep_law.rs`)**: `a_whole_model_extension_keeps_the_part_and_posts` passes while `a_whole_model_area_offset_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts` and `stock_source` keep pins stay intact.
- **Mutation checks**:
  - Reverted `boundary_ctx.rs` to `upstream/main`: `extension_*` pins in `adaptive_zero_margin_island` failed (3 failed); restored: passed.
  - Reverted `keep_law.rs` + `generate.rs` to `upstream/main`: `zero_margin_adaptive_around_island_names_uncut_stock_corners` failed (`generate notes missing corner warning`); restored: passed.
  - Reverted `script/api.rs` to `upstream/main`: `zero_margin_adaptive_around_island_names_uncut_stock_corners` failed (`generate exposes op notes`); restored: passed.
- **Clippy & Gate**:
  - `cargo xtask gate batch --only clippy` (`--all-targets -- -D warnings` across all workspace crates): passed in 366s.
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 200 of 202 steps passed (all `motion` suites + 140 of 142 `app` suites, including `adaptive_zero_margin_island` in 39s, `keep_law`, `narrow_band`, `adaptive_pinch`, `area_controls`, `area_overhead`, `setup_align_2d_area`, `mcp_verify`, `mcp_generate`).
  - `app:shoulder_adaptive::containment_outside_clears_past_the_edge_never_the_recess` failed its 60s timer under parallel gate load (81.90s) and passed when run alone (`47.97s`).
  - `app:stock_source_holes::framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` failed on a pre-existing `chamfer_ride::ride_loops` error (`has no wall under it`); re-running on unmodified branch base `7bcc13a4b` (`#2450`) produced the exact same failure in 0.01s.

## Goldens moved

None (`git diff --stat upstream/main` / `7bcc13a4b` on `*.nc` and `*.cl` is empty).

## Not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate release` (heavy `#[ignore]` lanes and UI snapshots; no UI code changed).
- Pre-existing failing test `stock_source_holes::framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` remains red from `#2450` on `upstream/main`.

## Overlaps

- `#2149` touches `crates/app/src/operation/boundary_ctx.rs` (`part_solid_of`, `area_ctx`, `op_stamp`) and `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (`Pocket`/`Offset2D`/`Pocket3D`), different functions/lines; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2253` touches `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (`Pocket`) and `crates/app/src/script/api.rs::op_view` (inside `if warnings`), different block/lines; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2460` and `#1713` touch `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (`Contour` and `Finish3D` arms), different lines; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2487` (merged to `upstream/main` after `7bcc13a4b`) touches `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs` line 124 (`contour_run_side`), different line from our line 142 (`unreached`).

Changelog: Whole-model and stock-source 2D clearing now reports unreached stock corners in notes (and MCP generate/verify) and keeps standing part islands blocked when extending outside the stock.
Fixes #2438

title: feat(post): carry a flipped WCS X or Y into the posted program
body:
## Why

The maintainer wrote (2026-11-17): "WCS54, X flipped - posting and generating are refused until the flip is cleared..  the ability to flip axis from a positive to negative is fundamental and should not be blocked.. posting and generation should take it into consideration rather.."

The maintainer decided on 2026-11-18, after the floor review: keep the meaning as built (the machine control runs a flipped axis reversed), and refuse probing in a flipped setup with a message that names the flip.

## What changed

- Generation, verification and the stock simulation no longer refuse a flipped setup. They stay in the setup frame, so the cut does not change.
- The job writes `PARAM WcsFlip` on each section of a flipped setup. A new post pass (`crates/post/src/post/wcs_flip.rs`) runs before `wcs_rotate` and `invert`. It mirrors the flipped axis about the work origin through `invert::translate_rules`.
- One flipped axis swaps G2/G3 and G41/G42. Two flipped axes (X and Y) keep them. Helix and canned cycles are carried.
- The flip composes with a machine-inverted axis.
- The travel check, the setup sheet and the viewport work envelope read the posted sign.
- `fanuc.cps` and `haas.cps` state `axisInversion = true` and name the flipped axes in the program header.
- Review fix (finding 2): a probe operation in a flipped setup is refused by name. The verification gate (`setup_wcs_flip::op_problem`) names the flipped axes and the probe operations. The post pass (`post::wcs_flip`) refuses a flipped section that holds probe records, so each stream builder is covered.
- Review fix (finding 4): the `refused` field of the MCP `set_wcs_flip` reply also names the operations of the setup that the post refuses (`setup_wcs_flip::setup_post_problems`).
- Review fix (finding 3): the WCS page note says that the machine control must run the flipped axis reversed, and that probing does not post. The status line names the refusal in place of "mirrored" when the post refuses the flip. The page note does not yet read the refusal of a rotated WCS or an unverified post: follow-up #2497 (the note must not load the post script each frame).

## Cases

Carried: Flip X, Flip Y, and Flip X+Y on 3-axis mill sections, with Fanuc and Haas.

Refused by name, with the flip as the cause:

- a flipped Z (follow-up #2474)
- a script without `axisInversion = true` (follow-up #2475)
- a flip together with a WCS rotation (follow-up #2476)
- probing (the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-18)
- turning, threading, live tool, ABC/tilt, EDM, wire and plasma sections
- a section that uses a modal origin or start across a change of flip
- a `WcsFlip` value that the pass cannot read

The decision file `docs/decisions/1649-wcs-flip-carry.md` has the case table and the reasons. Its new section "Probing in a flipped setup" records the probing decision and the dropped option (mirrored probing).

## Screenshots

Headless renders (egui_kittest, wgpu, 320 x 900) of the WCS page after a click on Flip Y. "Before" uses the UI files of `origin/main`. No GUI process was started.

| Before (origin/main) | After (this branch) |
|---|---|
| ![WCS page before](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/screenshots/pr-2492/wcs-flip-note-before.png?raw=true) | ![WCS page after](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/screenshots/pr-2492/wcs-flip-note-after.png?raw=true) |

## Pinning tests

- `crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs` (15 tests), for example `a_flipped_wcs_cuts_the_cam_path`, `one_flipped_axis_reverses_arcs_and_the_compensation_side_and_two_do_not`, `a_flipped_axis_on_an_inverted_machine_axis_posts_the_standard_signs`, `a_flipped_z_refuses_by_name`, `a_flipped_and_rotated_section_refuses_by_name`. title: fix(post): assign stable tool numbers on add, import, and project load
body:
### What changed
- `AddTool::new` assigns the lowest unused controller number in `1-99999` (`tool_numbers::next_free`), stores it on `ToolDef::number`, and exposes `AddTool::number()`.
- `ImportTools::with_options` allocates sequential unused numbers (`tool_numbers::next_free_from`) for every newly added or renamed tool while keeping existing and replaced tools' numbers reserved during the batch.
- `project::apply::check_and_apply` freezes legacy unnumbered `EntityKind::Tool` records to their 1-based name-sorted list position on load without emitting load notes.
- `SetToolNumber::new` refuses `None` by tool name so tools always keep an explicit number, while permitting the same number across disjoint setup machines (`setup_mount::machine_of`).
- `tool_numbers::numbers` assigns the lowest unused number to any stray raw `ToolDef { number: None }` entity so unnumbered test fixtures never collide with numbered tools.
- `add_tool` returns `number` and `posts_as` over MCP, UI add status displays `(T{number})`, `tool_settings` clamps existing tools to `1..=MAX`, `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` documents the updated MCP contract, and `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/build.camscript` adds its tools in `T1`/`T2`/`T3` order.

### Cause
- `AddTool` and `ImportTools` left `ToolDef::number` as `None`.
- `tool_numbers::numbers` fell back to each unnumbered tool's 1-based index in `model::named_entities`, so adding, renaming, or deleting a tool renumbered other tools between posts.

### Tests
- Pinning tests (red on `upstream/main`, green after fix):
  - `tool_numbers::adding_an_earlier_sorting_tool_keeps_posted_t_and_h_words`
  - `tool_numbers::deleting_an_earlier_tool_keeps_remaining_posted_t_and_h_words`
  - `tool_numbers::legacy_unnumbered_project_keeps_posted_numbers_after_add_and_delete`
  - `tool_numbers::importing_earlier_sorting_tool_keeps_existing_numbers`
- Mutation checks:
  - Reverted `AddTool::apply` to `number: None`: `adding_an_earlier_sorting_tool_keeps_posted_t_and_h_words` failed (red), then passed on restore (green).
  - Reverted `ImportTools::apply` `Step::Add` to `number: None`: `tool_import_modes::update_adds_unmatched_and_skips_identical_in_one_undo` failed (red), then passed on restore (green).
  - Reverted `project/apply.rs` to `upstream/main`: `legacy_unnumbered_project_keeps_posted_numbers_after_add_and_delete` failed (red), then passed on restore (green).
  - Reverted `commands/tool_number.rs` to `upstream/main`: `tool_numbers::a_number_is_set_refused_to_clear_and_walked_by_undo_and_redo` and `setup_mounts_post::a_tool_number_shared_across_machines_posts_but_clashes_within_one` failed (red), then passed on restore (green).
- Gate after review fix (`f1ed9b6e7aa1a4ea39a8ca14047c3d0ce11a47e8`):
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 92/93 steps passed, 11.2 minutes. The sole failure is the existing #2483 Linux wrap motion-line-count mismatch (`3246 != 3245`). The new tool-number pin and indexed fixture test pass. Across suites: 2,360 passed, 1 failed, 18 ignored.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed with no warnings.

### Goldens moved
- None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).
- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/build.camscript` reorders `add_tool` calls to match the committed `first-part.nc` tool numbers (`DR-0600` T1, `EM-0600-4FL` T2, `EM-1000-4FL` T3).

### Not exercised
- `cargo xtask gate batch` was not run after the final edit (all 27 golden `.nc` suites ran cleanly prior to reverting an intermediate `wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc` edit, and `example_catalog` + `first_4axis_part` + `first_router_part` passed).
- The full wrapped microARC golden test has the existing Linux motion-line-count failure tracked by #2483. The wrap fixture now explicitly preserves the committed tool table: `BN 1/8` T1, `EM 1/4 3FL` T2, `EM 1/8 2FL` T3. `wrapped_fixture_keeps_golden_tool_numbers` pins all posted tool comments and T/H lines independently of motion-line count. Removing that fixture table fails the pin; restoring it passes. The indexed microARC program also passes unchanged.

### Overlaps

Process change: yes
Changelog: Assign stable lowest-unused tool numbers at tool creation, import, and legacy project load (#2442)


### UI before and after (review finding 2)

Real UI renders of the same catalog tool added through the UI command queue, then opened in the tool editor. The before image uses the parent product sources. The after image uses this PR's product sources. Images live only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

Before: tool number `0` means list position; add status has no T number.

![Before: tool number editor and add status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/413bf75d50bb172d460f393f995634991ca64d1d/2488/tool-number-before.png)

title: fix(2d): join open contour runs and handle inside corners
body:
## What changed

- Added `camcraft_geometry::boundary_chains::join_open_runs` to deduplicate XY-coincident open runs regardless of direction and weld touching runs end to end. Single-point and non-finite runs pass through unchanged so operation generation refuses them by name.
- Called `join_open_runs` on `chains` in `selection_geometry_impl` (`crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs`) for `OpParams::Contour`, `OpParams::PlasmaProfile`, and `OpParams::WireContour`.
- Added `pub fn offset_run_side` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_run_side.rs` and re-exported it in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`. Both `contour_run_side::offset_run` and `crates/app/src/operation/contour_open.rs` (`offset_run`) now call it.
- Filtered `Region::sweep` loops to one outer CCW loop so inner CW holes from bridged bottleneck notches do not abort the offset.
- Added `corner_sector_left` for acute convex join arcs wrapping past 90 deg, `CAP_TIE` (`0.006 mm`) for arc-sag tie-breaking, and `nearest_on_run` clearance checks before inserting perpendicular `normal_at` endpoints on short inside-corner legs.
- Added decision record `docs/decisions/2277-contour-inside-corners.md`.

## Cause

- `stitch_open_runs` only closes full rings into `loops`, so manually picked open contour edges remained separate runs. Offsetting each run on its own drove the tool across inside corners into adjacent walls (`Z 0.000 near (40.000, 10.995)` on the U-notched block).
- On connected open chains, `offset_run` rejected inner CW holes across bridged bottleneck notches, misclassified acute convex join arcs with `cross`, added swallowed `normal_at` endpoints on short legs, and lost end-cap intersections within Clipper2's `5 um` arc sag.
- `crates/app/src/operation/contour_open.rs` carried a duplicate `offset_run` with the same defects.

## Tests

### Pins

- `camcraft-geometry` (`8 passed; 0 failed` in `boundary_chains`, new unit test):
  - `boundary_chains::tests::join_open_runs_welds_out_of_order_and_deduplicates_coincident_runs`
- `camcraft-motion` (`11 passed; 0 failed` in `contour_run_side`; 3 pins failed on unchanged `upstream/main`):
  - `machining2d::contour_run_side::tests::an_open_run_with_a_short_leg_at_an_inside_corner_stops_clear`
  - `machining2d::contour_run_side::tests::an_open_run_with_a_bottleneck_notch_bridges_the_mouth`
  - `machining2d::contour_run_side::tests::an_open_run_with_sharp_or_filleted_inside_corner_and_acute_turn_leaves_tool_radius`
- `camcraft-app` (`6 passed; 0 failed` in `contour_open_side`; 4 pins failed on unchanged `upstream/main`):
  - `u_notch_picked_open_edges_turn_inside_corners`
  - `filleted_inside_corner_smaller_than_tool_radius_succeeds_as_open_runs`
  - `acute_inside_corner_and_oversized_tool_succeed_open_and_closed`
  - `a_contour_open_boundary_with_a_short_inside_corner_leg_stops_clear`

### Mutations

- Reverting `join_open_runs` in `crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs`: 3 pins failed in `contour_open_side`; restoring passed 6/6.
- Reverting `offset_run` in `crates/app/src/operation/contour_open.rs`: 1 pin failed in `contour_open_side`; restoring passed 6/6.
- Reverting CCW loop filtering in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_run_side.rs`: 1 pin failed in `contour_run_side`; restoring passed 11/11.
- Removing `corner_sector_left`: 3 pins failed in `contour_run_side`; restoring passed 11/11.
- Bypassing `clear` on `normal_at` endpoints: 1 pin failed in `contour_run_side`; restoring passed 11/11.
- Bypassing `CAP_TIE`: 1 pin failed in `contour_run_side`; restoring passed 11/11.

### Gate and Clippy

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (858 batch test and lint steps across crate runs): `geometry` 15/15, `kernel` 14/14, `cl` 5/5, `tools` 6/6, `post` 86/86, `sim` 81/81, `motion` 94/94, `ui` 23/23, and `clippy -D warnings` 1/1 passed. `app` passed 532/533 steps.
- `app suites: microarc_test_part` failed `a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` (`wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc: line count 3246 != 3245`). That failure is pre-existing on `upstream/main` (`983f527bd`, upstream `post-merge` run `44258092076` from PR #2386 commit `eba0e477d`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

## Goldens moved

- None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Batch-excluded slow binaries (`motion:finish3d`, `motion:pivot5d`, `motion:flow`, `app:center_cut_multiaxis`) and release-mode suites did not run locally.
- Interactive mouse edge picking in the UI viewport did not run directly; integration tests pass `GeoSel::edge` picks through `App`.

## Overlaps

- `crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs`: PR #2484, PR #2433, and PR #2256 touch different functions (`drive_chains`, `selection_geometry_in`) than `selection_geometry_impl`. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`: PR #2460 and PR #2149 touch different exports and modules than `offset_run_side`. Whichever merges second refreshes.
