title: fix(motion): 2D Contour tab width is the bridge that stays, not the centre-path gap
body:
## What changed

2D Contour tabs now leave a bridge of the tab width that the user sets.

- `ring::tab_window` (new): the start tab window on the tool-centre ring is `tab_width + tool_diameter`. `tab_bridge::fit_tabs` grows it at corners and for leads (see "Review fixes"). Before, it was `tab_width` alone. The cutter disc removes `D/2` more material past each window end, so the bridge on the channel centre line was `tab_width - D`. A tab width of `D` or less left no bridge, and the part came free with no message.
- `tab_bridge.rs` (new): when the tab windows fill the whole loop, or no bridge of the tab width fits, the tabbed levels of that loop cut nothing. The operation shows a note that starts with `tabs:`. Before, this was silent.
- `contour.rs` calls `tab_bridge::cached` and `keep_cut` (506 lines; it was 517 before this PR).

## Readings

- Square 40 x 40, 6 mm cutter, outside contour, bottom level tabbed:
  - 4 tabs of 6 mm: four bridges of 6.0 mm (before: none).
  - 4 tabs of 5 mm: four bridges of 5.0 mm (before: none, the cuts overlapped by 1 mm).
  - 3 tabs of 10 mm: three bridges of 10.0 mm (before: 4 mm).
- `tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor`: the tabbed level is `4 x (6 + 10) = 64` mm shorter than the full ring (measured 64.0017 mm; the 1.7 um comes from window ends that fall on corner arcs).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/tests/contour_tabs.rs` (new): measures each bridge as the swept disc of the posted feeds against points on the tool-centre ring. Five tests, including the fill note.
- `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs`:
  - `tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor`: new length.
  - `contour_tabs_stand_down_the_entry_arms` and `contour_hop_rides_the_tall_tab_top`: these used four 6 mm tabs with a 10 mm tool on a 40 mm centre ring. No tab can stand there. They now use two 4 mm tabs; their asserts did not change.
- `crates/app/tests/first_router_part.rs`: in `examples/first-router-part.camproj`, only the cached moves of `2D Contour1` change (see "Review fixes"). The format version and the drill note come from main.
- `crates/app/tests/first_part_programs.rs`: `examples/first-router-part.nc` is recorded again with `camcraft-cli process`. Only the `2D Contour1` tab-gap lines change (lines 116-148).

## Gate

First version (b755c8e). The current gate is in "Review fixes". `cargo xtask gate quick`: 22 steps, 0 failed (motion lib and the touched motion suites, app `arc_entry`, `solid_law_goldens`, `wall_arc_entry`). Then `first_router_part`: 4 passed after the regenerate. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine.
- Control compensation (G41/G42) rings use the same window; on a straight wall the bridge is the same. Not measured separately.
- Wire EDM tabs (`wire_edm/tabs.rs`) are a different law and are not changed.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2480-tab-bridge-width.md`.

## Review fixes (maintainer, commit 613ba4abf)

The review found two blockers. The rule is now on the true material: the smallest distance between the swept discs on the two sides of a tab, with the leads included, is at least `W - tol`.

- **B1, corners.** A window of `W + D` measures arc length on the centre line. At a corner the chord is shorter, so the true neck fell under `W` with no message.
- **B2, leads.** Linear, Arc and Tangential leads reach back into the tab window and cut into the bridge with no message.

Choices (`docs/decisions/2480-tab-bridge-width.md`, "Review fixes"):

- B1: grow the windows until the true neck is `W`. Moving the tab centres was considered and dropped.
- B2: widen the windows by the lead reach. Refusing leads with tabs was considered and dropped.
- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_bridge.rs`: `fit_tabs` grows each window in bounded rounds (64 at most). Each round measures the keep tail (walk end and lead-out) against the next keep head (lead-in and walk start). The fit is cached per ring for each band.
- `ring::tabs_fill_note` is replaced by `tabs:` notes in `tab_bridge.rs`. When the windows fill the loop, the operation shows a note. This is a note, not a refusal.

Measured, square 40 x 40, D 6, 4 tabs, smallest bridge (before -> after):

| Lead | W 3 | W 6 | W 10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | 3 -> 3 | 6 -> 6 | 10 -> 10 |
| Perpendicular 4 | 3 -> 3 | 6 -> 6 | 10 -> 10 |
| Linear 4 | -5 -> 3 | -2 -> 6 | 2 -> 10 |
| Arc r3 | -3 -> 3 | 0 -> 6 | 4 -> 10 |
| Tangential r2 | -1 -> 3 | 2 -> 6 | 6 -> 10 |

Corners: inside 10 x 10 corner -0.10 -> 4.10 (W 4); picked start on an outside corner, W 4: 1.42 -> 4.0; W 1.5: -> 1.5; bore: 3.82 -> 4.13 (W 4).

Pins (`crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_bridge.rs`, new):

- `inside_corner_tabs_keep_the_tab_width`
- `outside_tab_centred_on_a_corner_from_a_picked_start`
- `bore_tabs_keep_the_tab_width`
- `every_lead_family_keeps_the_tab_width`
- `inside_and_conventional_straight_walls_keep_the_tab_width`

Red proof: with the initial `W + D` windows only, 5 of these tests fail (inside corner -0.10, picked corner 1.42, inside straight with Arc -1.0, Linear W 3 -5.0, bore 3.82). This includes (a) and the lead case.

Old pins that follow the wider windows:

- `contour_tabs.rs`: the `at_least` comment now says that it measures the centre-line run. `a_wide_tab_keeps_its_full_width` accepts a longer run where a tab sits on a corner arc.
- `machining2d.rs::tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor`: the held length is 64.64 mm, not 64, because the window ends on corner arcs grow.
- `machining2d.rs::contour_tabs_stand_down_the_entry_arms`: the tabs sat on the corners of the 10 x 10 inside ring with a neck of -0.10 mm (no bridge). Now they grow, and the floor walks round the two other corners as flat arcs. The helix check skips flat arcs.

Example: `examples/first-router-part.camproj` changes only in the cached moves of 2D Contour1. The keep ends move 3 mm from each tab (the Arc r3 lead reach). The stamp and the other operations are not changed.

Gate:

- `contour_tab_bridge` 5/5, `contour_tabs` 5/5, `machining2d` 68/68, `contour_whole` 8/8, motion lib machining2d 208 passed, `first_router_part` 4/4.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick`: 120 steps, 118 passed. Two failed: app `thread_boss` and `thread_mill`. Their `.nc` goldens are stale (tool numbers T01/T03 swapped). The same test fails on the PR head b755c8e without this commit, so it is not from this change.

Not exercised: no air cut; G41/G42 rings not measured; `blend_turns` fillets with tabs not pinned; whole-model bands only through `contour_whole`; band boundaries (#2460) not changed; the time of the 64 rounds not measured.

### Second review (head 62815c223)

Both reviews of 613ba4abf had one blocker: `examples/first-router-part.nc` was stale.

- Main (9d6b57c09, with #2560) is merged into the branch. The merge had no conflict.
- `examples/first-router-part.nc` is recorded again with `camcraft-cli process`. Against main, 25 lines change (lines 116-148), all `2D Contour1` tab gaps. Example: `Y86.991` -> `Y80.991`. The G73 line stays as main recorded it. No guide or site page quotes the changed lines.
- `tab_bridge.rs`: a NaN bridge distance counts as short (`gap.is_nan() || gap < need - SLACK`).
- `tab_bridge.rs`: if `count * (W + D)` is at least the loop length, the fit gives the fill note before it reserves one entry for each tab.
- `contour_tab_bridge.rs`: the fixtures that fit assert `n == count`. New test `a_huge_tab_count_fills_the_loop_without_a_huge_allocation` (`u32::MAX` tabs).
- The decision file records the known limit N2: the fit compares only neighbouring cuts within `W + D` of each walk end.

Gate on 62815c223:

| Binary | Result |
|---|---|
| motion `contour_tab_bridge` | 6 passed |
| motion `contour_tabs` | 5 passed |
| motion `machining2d` | 68 passed |
| motion `contour_whole` | 8 passed |
| motion `contour_start` | 21 passed |

title: perf(xtask): run release-gate suites in a longest-first queue; narrow the alone list
body:
Process change: yes

For the maintainer's decision - a process change (xtask). Measured before/after on the same Hetzner ccx43 (16 cores): numbers follow in a comment.

## Why

On a 16-core server the release gate used every core for the ~10 min of builds, then ~80% of the run used one or two cores. Three causes in `xtask/src`: `lanes::alone()` sent every camcraft-app / camcraft-kernel step to run alone, one after another; `lanes::waves` grouped the other steps into barrier waves that each waited for their slowest lane; and the alone steps used the default budget of 6.

## What changed

- **A. A narrower alone list** (`lanes.rs`). Builds (`--no-run`), clippy, every UI step (`in_ui` or camcraft-ui) and an app/kernel step that is not one named target still run alone. Of the single app/kernel targets, only `lanes::ISOLATED` runs alone. Every other app/kernel target now joins the shared lanes.
- **B. A work queue in place of barrier waves** (new `queue.rs`). The builds run first, each alone. Then `budget::lane_limit` lanes of `budget::per_lane` jobs each pull the next step as they finish. The alone steps run last, one at a time, with the whole budget. The queue runs the longest steps first (Graham's LPT rule), using the per-step seconds the previous release run wrote to `gate-logs/release-*/timings.tsv`. Every release run now writes that file. A step with no recorded time ranks with the longest, and with no history at all the queue keeps plan order.
- The checkout guard (VOID) now runs before every queued step. A failed build still stops the run, and a failed suite still stops nothing.
- **C. Alone steps use the whole budget for `--test-threads`.** This already happens through `budget::scale` (the plan's `6` is the default budget). The gate now prints a note when the machine has more cores than the budget, because `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16` is what lets a 16-core runner use all its cores. **cut.yml should set it.**
- `--dry-run` still prints the whole plan, with the queue in the order the lanes pull it. On this tree that is 2 builds, 1019 queued steps and ~60 alone steps.

## The named alone list (`lanes::ISOLATED`) and why

These are the targets whose tests assert on wall-clock time, so a busy neighbour could turn them red. They were found by grepping the suites for `recv_timeout`, `deadline`, `Instant`/`elapsed` and `Duration::from_secs`. Suites that only print a timing are not listed.

- `app:lib` and `kernel:lib`: watchdogs in the libs' own tests (`step_guard_tests`, `step_division_tests`, `solidcore_step`)
- `app:import_step_closed_shell`, `import_step_corner_blend`, `import_step_curve_guard`, `import_step_guard`, `import_step_guard_default_cap`, `import_step_open_shell`: STEP import watchdogs (`within(limit, ..)` panics on a timeout)
- `app:large_models` (streaming import < 60 s), `mcp_live` (TCP deadlines of 0.3-20 s), `shoulder_adaptive` (< 60 s), `step_nesting` (refusal < 1 s), `stock_field_cost` (per-program budget), `stock_play`, `stock_play_partial`, `stock_play_precalc` (worker deadlines)
- `kernel:heal_import`, `import_corpus`, `mesh_deviation_bench`, `solidcraft_hostile`, `solidcraft_import`, `step_agreement`, `step_import`: built on the `step_util` / `smb_util` watchdogs

A new suite with a wall-clock assertion has to be added to this list. A test pins that every listed binary exists.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p xtask`: all pass (161 unit tests plus the integration binaries). These tests were rewritten for the queue: lanes (schedule split, the ISOLATED entries exist, target keys, longest-first order, history picks the newest release `timings.tsv`), the executor fixture (overlap, failure, build stop, VOID), and budget (the per-lane `-j` and test-thread sums stay within the budget, and alone steps get the full budget).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not exercised: a full release gate run. That is the measurement in the comment to follow.

## Risks

- More app/kernel binaries now run beside each other, so peak memory is higher (the app heavy release lanes especially). The suites already use per-process temp dirs (`std::process::id()`), and that was spot-checked.
- A timing-sensitive test missed by the grep could flake under load. Adding it to `ISOLATED` fixes that.

## Revert

Revert this commit. The plan steps themselves are unchanged, so nothing else depends on it. To get back only the old alone rule, make `lanes::alone` return true for any `camcraft-app` / `camcraft-kernel` argument.

`PROCESS_VERSION` is not bumped here; the merging session bumps it.

title: fix(ui): persist desktop GPU startup diagnostics
body:
## What changed

Desktop startup appends plain-text diagnostics to the platform configuration folder's `camcraft.log`.
Each record synchronizes to disk before returning.
Startup keeps the previous run's records.
The file keeps INFO diagnostics when terminal logging is off.
GPU enumeration, candidate and selection records name the adapter, vendor, device, backend and driver.
Panic and returned startup failures keep forced backtraces.
Crash messages name the log file and backend flags to try.
The panic hook preserves the previous hook.
The CLI keeps its stderr-only initializer.

## Cause

The desktop entry point installed only a stderr subscriber.
A Windows launch without a terminal had no persistent diagnostics.
Adapter descriptors discarded driver metadata.
Returned startup failures had no persistent backtrace.

## Tests

These six pins failed on unchanged production code and pass with the fix:

- `desktop_startup_error_survives_without_a_terminal`
- `desktop_startup_error_is_persisted_when_terminal_logging_is_off`
- `desktop_startup_log_preserves_the_previous_run`
- `desktop_panic_keeps_its_message_and_backtrace`
- `startup_adapter_log_names_the_gpu_backend_and_driver`
- `startup_gpu_refusal_names_backend_retry_flags`

`desktop_log_open_failure_keeps_a_named_terminal_diagnostic` also passes.
The panic pin checks repeated initialization, the previous hook and INFO persistence with terminal logging off.
All ten mutations failed at runtime and passed after restoration:

- Restore upstream's desktop entry point.
- Restore upstream's GPU descriptor, refusal and bring-up code.
- Omit the panic file write.
- Omit the previous panic hook call.
- Truncate the previous log instead of appending.
- Apply the terminal's off filter to the file layer.
- Omit the returned startup failure's backtrace.
- Omit returned-error logging in main.
- Omit backend retry hints.
- Omit the stderr subscriber fallback after a log-open failure.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 13 steps.
Separate `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
`git diff --check upstream/main` passed.
Every diff hunk has a written justification outside the repository.
The decision record is `docs/decisions/2421-startup-log-uma.md`.

## Goldens moved

None.
`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

Validation ran headlessly on Linux.
Windows message boxes, physical GPU failures and survival of a full system lock were not exercised.
File synchronization follows `write_all` in the implementation; the tests do not simulate power loss.
No batch gate, release gate or browser build ran.

## Overlaps

PR #1798 touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_window.rs`.
It changes shell construction and capture state.
This PR changes `Shell::fail` and `refuse_dialog`.
It touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
PR #2110 has merged, so this branch does not stack on it.
This branch starts from upstream/main `5f2c3bf4b`.

Effort: medium (no escalation).

Changelog: Desktop startup persists GPU adapter and driver diagnostics, panic and failure backtraces, and log-location and backend-retry guidance.

Fixes #2421


## Startup error dialog screenshots

These are native Linux dialog captures from an isolated `rfd`/zenity harness.

## What changed

Dropdowns read `menu_width`, `recent_width`, `menu_gap`, and `menu_pad_x` from the theme.

The built-in tables and file overlay move into child modules to keep the theme modules near 400 lines.

Dropdown drawers used fixed dimensions and repeated row insets.

title: fix(chamfer): no-pick 2D Chamfer rides the wall; verify holds its tip to it
body:
## What changed

**Generator (no-pick 2D Chamfer).** The ride sectioned the model at Top of Part Z and put the cone tip on that outline at the corner depth. On a model whose edge already carries a modelled chamfer, that outline is the bevel's *top* edge, which sits inside the wall by the bevel's width. The cone then cut a V 0.71 mm into the part (QA p01-flange: `G1 X75 Y15.999 Z-3`, which is world y -14.001 against a wall at y -15), and the width moved only Z. Now `material_source` sections the source twice, at the top plane (the edges to break) and at the corner depth `top - width*tan(angle)` (the wall). The new `machining2d::chamfer_ride_loops` gives each top loop the wall loop within `width` of it. For a vertical wall the two loops are the same and the top loop itself is ridden, so sharp-edged parts post exactly as before. A top edge with no wall within the width (a blind pocket or island shallower than the chamfer depth) is refused by name, with the spot.

**Verify (program sim).** The V passed because the op's edge-break record declared that same false edge, and any declared bevel got credit. A 2D Chamfer's records are now credited only where the cone tip stands on a wall: at every sample along the edge, the model's top 0.05 mm off the edge, on at least one side, must be no higher than the tip plus the verdict tolerance (`sim::stock_sim::on_walls`, new `wall_anchor.rs`). A record that fails is dropped and logged, and its columns are judged against the model, so the cut is a blocking gouge. Deburr records are not held to this: a deburr may legitimately break an obtuse 3D edge, such as a drafted wall. `program_breaks` moved from `stock_sim.rs` to `stock_sim_breaks.rs`, and `Planned` gained `walled`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/2435-chamfer-modelled-edge.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, each mutation-checked:
- `crates/app/tests/chamfer_modelled_edge.rs` (new). The model is a 40x20x10 brick with a modelled 1x45 chamfer on its top edges. It is the stock and the part, and one no-pick 2D Chamfer runs on it.
  - `a_no_pick_chamfer_on_a_modelled_chamfer_rides_the_wall`: width 1. Every feed tip is at z 9 on the wall (x ±20 / y ±10), and the gate is clean.
  - `the_width_moves_the_tip_along_the_bevel_not_only_in_z`: width 0.5. Tips are at z 9.5 on the bevel (±19.5 / ±9.5), and the gate is clean.
  - `a_cone_tip_inside_the_part_is_a_gouge_not_edge_break_credit`: the old ride and its record are put back by hand, and the gate must report a gouge.
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests` (4 unit tests: vertical wall unchanged, bevel rides the wall, too-far wall refuses, lower edge ignored).
- `stock_sim::wall_anchor::tests` (2 unit tests: tip on the wall keeps its credit, tip inside loses it).

Mutations:
- Generator fix reverted (ride the top section again): the two ride tests fail. With the fixed verify, the old ride is convicted end to end: `gouge ... 1175 cell(s), worst 0.94 mm`.
- Wall filter disabled (`walled` ignored): the gouge test fails, because the gate passes the V.

QA part (p01-flange, from the issue), run through `camcraft-cli process`:
- No-pick width 1 now posts `X75 Y15 Z-3` (world y -15, z 14), with the gate ok.
- Width 0.5 posts `Y15.5 Z-2.5`, with the gate ok.
- The old ride, with this verify, is blocked: `gouge ... worst 1.00 mm` (w 1) and `worst 0.50 mm` (w 0.5).
- The issue's picked-chain workaround project still posts, with the gate ok.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` : green, 215 steps, 0 failed (17.4 min), among them chamfer_modelled_edge, edge_break_gate, edge_break_bound, golden_cl, mill2d_b, setup_align_chamfer, setup_carry_credits, stock_chamfer_added_part, posting, solid_law_goldens, verify, and the motion and sim lib unit tests, plus `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The tilted (3+2) frame variant of the no-pick chamfer. The corner depth is taken in the frame's own Z, the same as the top plane, but no tilted test was added.
- Curved bevels (a modelled round under a chamfer) beyond the QA STEP's R5 corners.
- The UI. Pixel snapshots are untouched.
- Windows/Linux.
- The release-lane heavy suites.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer with no picked edges on a model whose edge is already chamfered now rides the wall under the bevel (the tip no longer cuts a V into the part), and verify now blocks a 2D Chamfer whose cone tip stands inside the part instead of crediting it as the edge break (#2435)

Effort: high (no escalation)
Fork synced at: branched from upstream main abe24ff09

Fixes #2435

title: fix(sim): pack the playback picture's base from the uncut stock
body:
## What changed

The simulation's stock body was never visible in v0.23.0 (#2396).

**Cause.** #2181 (the stock removal calculated before playback) moved the playback worker's `PackedBase::of` call after the calculation. The calculation leaves the playback at the end of the program. `PackedBase::of` runs the eikonal pass, which writes `max(mesh, cut)` into the mesh layer, and later frames can only lift cells over it. So the GPU eye's base was the **finished** part, and every frame at every playhead drew the finished part. When a program machines the part to size, that body sits inside the model, so no stock is seen.

**Fix.** `crates/app/src/stock_play_worker.rs`: the base is packed from the uncut stock before the calculation runs, as it was before #2181. This is a one-line move with a comment. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2396-sim-stock-visible.md`.

## How tested

- Pinning test `crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs::the_picture_at_the_start_is_the_uncut_stock_after_the_calculation`. It spawns the worker with the calculation, waits for `Ready` and takes the packed frame at move 0. It asserts that the composed lattice the eye draws (`max(base.mesh, cut) < 0`) holds the uncut stock's material, and that the base mesh layer is the uncut stock's bit for bit.
  - Before the fix: FAILED, `move 0 draws the uncut stock, not the finished part`, left 2016 (the finished part's texels), right 2880 (the uncut stock's).
  - After the fix: ok.
- The whole `stock_play_precalc` suite passes (8 pass, 1 heavy lane ignored).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 4481c2a06: green (app lib, stock_play, stock_play_partial, stock_play_precalc; 5 steps, 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The windowed app on a GPU. The test reads the packed lattice the GPU eye uploads, not pixels, so the shader composite is not run.
- The maintainer's own project. The fixture is the #2181 suite's staged face with a part cube, where the finished stock equals the part.
- No pixel snapshots were run or changed.

Changelog: Simulation draws the stock body again: playback started from the finished part, hidden inside the model, after the removal was calculated before playback (#2396)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #2396

title: fix(app): support 5-axis and rotary operations in aligned setups
body:
Based on `upstream/main` `3e47b898b`.

## What changed
- Updated `selection::drive_chains` in `crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs` and `operation::material_region::drive_chains_of` in `crates/app/src/operation/material_region.rs` to transform picked edges through `setup_align::pose_in`.
- Updated `fixture::rotary_axis_of` in `crates/app/src/fixture.rs` to read facets through `setup_align::facets_in`.
- Added `Contour5D`, `Parallel5D`, `Swarf`, `AdvancedSwarf`, `RotaryContour`, `RotaryParallel`, `RotaryOffset`, `MultiAxisRough`, `Flow5D`, and `MultiAxisContour` to `setup_align::verified_kind` in `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs`.
- Updated `setup_align::generation_problem` and module documentation to list all ten verified kinds.
- Added nine pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/setup_align_multiaxis.rs` and recorded decisions in `docs/decisions/2286-aligned-setup-multiaxis.md`.

## Cause
- `setup_align::verified_kind` refused all ten 5-axis and rotary operations in `generation_problem`.
- Two remaining world readers bypassed setup alignment: `selection::drive_chains` called `model::transform_of` for `MultiAxisContour` edges, and `fixture::rotary_axis_of` called `model::world_facets` to fit a rotary axis.

## Tests
- On unchanged `upstream/main`, `setup_align_multiaxis` failed (`0 passed; 7 failed`) at `setup_align::generation_problem`.
- All 9 tests in `crates/app/tests/setup_align_multiaxis.rs` pass (`38.41s`), matching `[90, 0, 90]` and oblique `[35, 25, 40]` aligned setups against baked parts across toolpaths (`from`, `to`, `axis`), posted NC programs, fitted rotary axes, fixed workholding clearance (`RotaryContour`), and divergence or refusal on the unaligned part:
  - `turned_contour5d_cuts_and_posts_like_the_baked_part`
  - `turned_parallel5d_cuts_and_posts_like_the_baked_part`
  - `turned_flow5d_cuts_and_posts_like_the_baked_part`
  - `turned_swarf_and_advanced_swarf_cut_and_post_like_the_baked_part`
  - `turned_multiaxis_rough_cuts_and_posts_like_the_baked_part`
  - `turned_rotary_contour_cuts_posts_and_fits_axis_like_the_baked_part`
  - `turned_rotary_parallel_cuts_posts_and_fits_axis_like_the_baked_part`
  - `turned_rotary_offset_cuts_posts_and_fits_axis_like_the_baked_part`
  - `turned_multiaxis_contour_routes_drive_chains_through_setup_frame`
- Mutation checks verified each code guard before the final doc-comment update:
  - Reverting `selection::drive_chains` to `model::transform_of` failed `turned_multiaxis_contour_routes_drive_chains_through_setup_frame` (`picked chain 1 stands at z -5.000, outside the window [1.500, 3.000]`); restoring `pose_in` passed (`2.73s`).
  - Reverting `fixture::rotary_axis_of` to `model::world_facets` failed `turned_rotary_parallel_cuts_posts_and_fits_axis_like_the_baked_part` (`RotaryParallel: axis [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]`); restoring `facets_in` passed (`9.40s`).
  - Removing the ten variants from `setup_align::verified_kind` failed all 9 `setup_align_multiaxis` tests (`0 passed; 9 failed`); restoring them passed all 9 (`197.41s`).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed after the final edit (`wall 11.2 min, 51 step(s), 0 failed`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed after the final edit with zero warnings.

## Goldens moved
None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised
- I did not run a real CNC machine or physical rotary controller.
- 5-axis tests posted on a synthetic A+B machine without rotary speed limits, and `RotaryContour` and `RotaryOffset` mounted `assets/machines/tilthead.mch` at post time after unmounted generation.
- Full `gate batch` and `gate release` suites outside the 51-step quick gate were not run.

## Overlaps
`crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs` is also changed by open PR #2256 (`needs-rework`, `conflicts`). PR #2256 modifies the `resolve_chain` call inside `drive_chains`, while this PR changes `drive_chains`'s `setup` parameter and the `setup_align::pose_in` lookup; whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Support all ten 5-axis and rotary operations in aligned setups, including turned drive chains and fitted rotary axes.

Fixes #2286

Color-vision selection belongs to each world, but its palette also reads the live theme ground.

body:
## What changed

- Replaced the blanket `kind != Kind::Mill` refusal in `setup_align::generation_problem` with a per-machine capability matrix (`verified_for_machine`).
- Enabled aligned-setup generation for all 12 turning kinds and `Drill` on `Kind::Lathe`, the 17 verified mill kinds plus all 12 turning kinds on `Kind::MillTurn`, `PlasmaProfile` on `Kind::Plasma`, `WireContour` on `Kind::WireEdm`, and `SinkerBurn` / `SinkerSideBurn` on `Kind::SinkerEdm`.
- Kept aligned-setup refusals active for `Kind::Waterjet`, unverified foreign operations on non-mill machines (naming that machine kind), `Probe`, 5-axis/rotary kinds, and `tilt().is_some()`.
- Routed 4-axis ruled wire picks in `operation::wire_ruled` through `setup_align::pose_in` using `op.setup`.
- Routed cavity electrode derivation (`operation::sinker_faces`, `pick::align::outward_normal`) through `setup_align::pose_in` and `facets_in`.
- Added `ElectrodeFromFaces::new_in` and updated MCP `electrode_from_faces` to forward an explicit setup name when given.
- Updated `an_aligned_setup_on_an_edm_names_the_edm_kind_it_is_refused_on` in `setup_align.rs` to assert the per-machine unverified-op refusal on EDM while leaving the machine-level refusal with `Waterjet`.

## Cause

`setup_align::generation_problem` rejected every machine kind other than `Kind::Mill` at the gate before operation generation ran. title: fix(ui): show tilted heights along the tool axis
body:
Stacked on #2418 (merge #2418 first)

## What changed

Tilted height planes now use the operation frame and the shared `fold_height` resolver.
The rectangle spans the stock in local XY.
Its corners and label anchors pass through `TiltedFrame::to_world`.
Height echoes and viewport labels state the local distance along the tool axis.
Draft tilt edits update these values before Apply.
Invalid tilts hide the planes and show the existing named refusal.
`operation::region_z` uses the same folded height.
Untilted planes and text retain their existing behavior.

The original stack used parent head `3e62cea0a`.
This branch also includes the requested pocket island and depth validation fixes from parent head `302b097254569c239d5d5e3f28ff06625080b92c`.
The display changes address #2416.
The decision record is `docs/decisions/2416-tilted-height-display.md`.

## Cause

The display resolved heights as setup Z and drew horizontal stock-XY rectangles.
It did not read the tilted tool axis.
On the asymmetric test stock, the correct clearance is 21 along the axis.
The old display placed a clearance corner at local height -5.
The old region read returned 10 instead of the fold coordinate 14.

## Tests before review fixes

Seven pins in `egui_app::heights_tests` failed before this fix:

- `tilted_height_planes_use_tool_axis_and_local_stock_corners`
- `tilted_height_echoes_use_tool_axis_on_asymmetric_stock`
- `invalid_draft_tilt_hides_height_planes_and_names_the_missing_direction`

- `tilted_height_echoes_follow_an_unapplied_tilt_edit`
- `tilted_fixed_height_echoes_keep_the_generation_origin_shift`
- `tilted_height_labels_show_local_axis_distance`

All 12 tests in the height suite pass.
The unchanged-code runs used the parent head before the #2416 fix.

Ten mutation checks failed, then passed after restoration:

- Restore the old region-height resolver.
- Restore the old plane rendering code.

- Replace local stock bounds with world bounds.
- Remove the origin-Z shift from plane placement.
- Remove draft tilt forwarding.
- Remove the invalid-frame guard from height planes.
- Remove the invalid-frame guard from the region-height read.
- Remove the invalid-frame guard from the height echo.
- Restore the old viewport label value.

The old region mutation retained the parent resolver adapter so the stack could compile.
The mutated region function matched upstream/main.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 253 steps, zero failures.
Clippy then requested an equivalent closure simplification.
All 12 height tests passed again after that change.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final code.

Effort: high for the review fixes. No escalation.

## Review fixes

Head: `26f2162873f3fd882ea35f5c1c0cf609c51dc073`.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed on this head.
Result: 253 steps, 3,198 tests passed, 27 ignored, zero failures.

The display cache retains local bounds and resolved heights for unchanged inputs.
Its key includes geometry allocations, placements, entity membership, setup definitions, source, height, and draft tilt.
Generation, verification, and posting do not read this cache.

`adaptive_entry_pieces::a_narrow_second_piece_names_its_ramp_stand_in_at_each_level`.

**Cause:** #2383 (for #2232) added `machining2d::pocket::non_sliver_center`.
It sent every multi-piece cutter-center area (two or more outer loops)
through a `Region::from_slices` rebuild, even when the sliver scan dropped
nothing. Clipper's normalisation restarts each loop at another vertex, so a
multi-piece pocket's pass starts moved. The narrow second piece's 1x1
center square started at (56, 6) instead of (56, 5), and the test's named
site no longer matched. The entry was still a named ramp (no gouge, no
unnamed plunge), but the move was an unintended side effect and not part of
#2232's decision.

**Fix:** `non_sliver_center` returns the plain `region.offset(-erode)`
unchanged unless at least one sliver is actually removed. Regions without
slivers now come out exactly as they did before #2383, and #2232's sliver
drop still applies where a sliver exists. Not a revert: #2383's stock-reach
clearing and sliver filter stay. The reasoning is in
`docs/decisions/2426-adaptive-entry-red.md`.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, on `3e47b898b`, the test fails with: `no named ramp stand-in for the pass start (56.000, 5.000) at Z -4.000 ... notes: ["entry: the pass start (56.000, 6.000) at Z -4.000 ... ramp along the pass instead", ...]`
- After the fix, all 5 tests of `adaptive_entry_pieces` pass.
- New pin `machining2d::pocket::non_sliver_tests::a_multi_piece_center_without_slivers_is_the_plain_offset` (motion lib) fails when the fix is disabled and passes with it.

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `e10ba5ba3`: 20 steps, 0 failed (motion lib incl. adaptive_troch tests that share `non_sliver_center`; motion adaptive_hsm, climb_direction, corner_arc_radius, corner_blend, entry_arc, optimal_load, predrilled_entry, refusal_ghost, rest_zigzag, rest2d, shape_masks, solid_law, top_z_level, xy_arc_entry; app pick_agnostic, pocket_overhead, solid_law_goldens).
- `adaptive_entry_pieces` (motion): 5/5 pass, including the failing test.
- `shoulder_adaptive` (app, #2383's own suite, pins the sliver drop and the outside-stock clearing): 9/9 pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

The release heavy lanes and the batch tier. The next post-merge run is the confirmation that #2426 asks for.

title: fix(operation): read a tilted op's reference heights along its tool axis
body:
## What changed

A tilted (3+1 / 3+2, `tilt.a_deg`/`b_deg`) operation took its reference heights - Top/Bottom of stock, Top/Bottom of model, Work offset - as the setup's world Z and only subtracted the plane origin's Z. It never measured along the turned tool axis. On #2389's bar (10 Y x 30 Z, centred on A) a Slot at A 90 with Top = Top of stock got 15 along the axis instead of 5, so it cut air. On other sides of an asymmetric stock it would plunge to the wrong depth.

- New `camcraft_app::operation::fold_height` (`crates/app/src/operation/tilt_heights.rs`). Under a non-upright tilt, each reference height is the referenced geometry's extent along the tool axis (`TiltedFrame::z_local` over its facets). It is returned as `z_local + origin.z`, so the existing `- origin.z` fold in `run_job` / `source_region` gives exactly the local value.
- Where it is used: the generation heights (`collect_job` through `resolve_params_folded`), the Contour/Pocket/Trace section plane (`section_z_of`) and the area-controls cut plane (`boundary_ctx`).
- Unchanged: Fixed heights keep the shipped `h - origin.z` law (pinned by `tilt.rs`). A Selection reference keeps the setup resolve, because a tilted op refuses a picked source first. Untilted ops and upright tilts (A0 B0) read the setup resolve verbatim, so prismatic paths and goldens keep their bits.
- `resolve_params` now delegates to `resolve_params_with` (the resolver is passed in). The refusal wording is unchanged.
- The viewport planes and the Heights tab's "(= Z ...)" echo are display-only and were split out to #2416 (P3, filed). Decision record: `docs/decisions/2389-tilt-heights-axis.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, in the new file `crates/app/tests/tilt_heights.rs`:
- `a_slot_at_a90_reads_top_of_stock_along_the_tool_axis`: the issue's proof. Clearance along the axis is 15 (main gives 25) and the bottom is 4.
- `an_offset_bar_reads_its_own_side_at_a_minus_90_and_the_underside`: an asymmetric stock (Y -1..11, Z -20..10) with a plane origin off the world origin.
  - A -90, origin (2,0,3): top 11; clearance 21 along the axis (main gives 17).
  - A0 B180, origin Z 3: top 23. This case also exercises the `+ origin.z` hand-off.
- `a_tilted_contour_sections_the_model_along_the_tool_axis`: a tilted Contour on a part, with Top/Bottom of model. On main it is refused with "no material at z = 14.000"; with the fix it contours at local 4..3.

Mutation check (revert, then restore):
- `collect_job` set back to the setup resolve: tests 1 and 2 go red (25 vs 15; 17 vs 21).
- `section_z_of` given no frame: test 3 goes red.
- `+ origin.z` dropped from `fold_height`: test 2 goes red (18 vs 21).
- With everything restored, all three are green.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 247 steps, 0 failed (14.6 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. It includes `first_4axis_part`, which holds `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` and `.nc` byte-for-byte (the round bar is symmetric about A, so it stays unchanged), plus `tilt`, `tilt_basis_compat`, `opframe_seam` and the heights suites.

## Not exercised

- The UI planes and echo (#2416).
- The post's `ClearancePlane` parameter for a tilted op still states the setup Z (`posting.rs`).
- `material_local.top` is still `material.top - origin.z`.
- A tilt at a non-right angle (e.g. A 45) on a round bar: the facet extent is the tessellation's, which can be up to one chord sagitta under the true cylinder.
- Bore/Thread under a tilt: they read the same height set, but no test covers them.
- No machine run.

Changelog: A tilted (3+2) operation now measures Top/Bottom of stock, Top/Bottom of model and Work offset heights along its tool axis, not as the setup's Z (#2389)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #2389 (the viewport planes and "(= Z ...)" text, #2416, finish it)

title: fix(post): refuse unsupported Sinumerik G84 and G85 dwells
body:
## What changed

Refuse positive Sinumerik G84 tapping and G85 reaming dwells by name.
Suppress the refused hole's expanded cutting moves.
Keep zero-dwell cycles available.

## Cause

The post silently dropped G84 dwell and wrote P on G85.
The normal drilling generator gives these cycles zero dwell.
The public stream serializer and parser accept positive dwell for both.
Siemens' [ISO dialects Function Manual, 07/2021, section 6.3, table 6-2](https://cache.industry.siemens.com/dl/files/254/109801254/att_1077768/v1/ONE_840Dsl_828D_iso_dialects_fct_man_0721_en-US.pdf) lists P on G84 and none on G85.
This fix uses the issue's allowed G84 refusal until the post supports its dwell encoding.

## Tests

- `sinumerik_g84_dwell_is_refused_by_name` failed before the fix and passes after it.
- `sinumerik_g85_dwell_is_refused_by_name` failed before the fix and passes after it.
- `sinumerik_g84_and_g85_without_dwell_still_post` passes.
- Pins cover 1 ms, 250 ms, and a hand-authored fractional millisecond.
- Restoring the upstream post makes each refusal pin fail. Restoring the fix makes all three tests pass.
- Removing refused-hole tracking makes both pins fail on leaked G1 cuts. Restoring it makes them pass.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 46 steps.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

The configured sccache wrapper stalled the initial build.
The checks completed with the wrapper disabled.

## Goldens moved

None.
`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

No physical controller ran this output.
G84 P output remains unsupported by this post.

## Overlaps

None found for the three changed files.
This branch starts from upstream/main 3e47b898b.

title: fix(2d): clear outside containment to stock on clearing ops
body:
Based on `upstream/main` `6349a542e` (`v0.23.0`).

## What changed
- Added `AreaCtx::outside_clearing_stock` and updated `reach_past_edge` and `resolve` in `crates/app/src/operation/boundary.rs` so closed clearing operations (`Family::Clearing`) with `Containment::Outside` and setup stock expand to `stock.offset(2.0 * r)` minus holes and islands.
- Guarded enclosed pockets in `reach_past_edge` with a `1e-2` mm rim check so pockets completely enclosed by part walls stay inside their walls instead of jumping to stock.
- Added `non_sliver_center` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs` and called it from `pocket_entered` and `adaptive_trochoidal_with` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch.rs`) to decompose pinched Clipper offset loops and drop sub-tolerance (`<= 0.01 mm^2` area and `<= 0.008 mm` half-width) slivers.
- Added `name_outside_entry_refusal` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs` to name `Extension (Boundary)` and setup stock when `Outside` clearing fails for lack of room or missing entry.
- Updated `crates/app/tests/shoulder_adaptive.rs` and recorded the architectural decision in `docs/decisions/2232-adaptive-outside-stock.md`.

## Cause
`reach_past_edge` grew closed clearing selections by `2 * r` even when setup stock surrounded the part. That left a cutter-center width of zero or sub-tolerance Clipper chord slivers after `-r` erosion, so `2D Adaptive` failed with `the center area has no room for an entry` or emitted empty-move toolpaths on curved or flush corners.

## Tests

title: docs(guide): continuous 4-axis walkthrough on the Tormach 770MX + microARC 4
body:
**Stacked on #2342** (`issue/796-tormach-wrapped-a`, Fixes #796). This branch starts from that PR's head `ef864e37d`; until #2342 merges, this PR's diff also shows its files. It merges after #2342. Fork synced at upstream main 4e8616b (through #2342's branch).

## What changed

The continuous half of #1904: a step-by-step guide page for the Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, with a committed demo project and drawn pictures.

- **Page:** `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-continuous-4axis-part.md`, "Your first continuous 4-axis program". It covers: how the bar is held; the machine file's four A values (axis, travel, `nose_to_axis`, A rate) and what to compare with the machine; finding the A centreline and setting G54 on it; the ball tool; a Rotary Parallel operation, setting by setting; the checks and what the stock simulation says; the posted program read line by line; what the post refuses; a run in the PathPilot simulator; then a single-block start and an air cut with no bar.
- **What the post writes, in plain words, from the Hub readings on #796:** `G93` on a feed that turns A with X Y Z, and why (reading 2: in `G94` F is the X Y Z distance only; reading 3: `G93` is accepted and timed); the A rate cap worked out on real lines; an A-only feed in `G94` with F in degrees per minute (reading 4); A counting on through 180 (reading 1); `G94` back before the last rapid.
- **Demo project:** `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj`, the program it posts `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc` (3213 lines) and the model `examples/models/first-continuous-4axis-part.obj` (made by `gen_first_continuous_4axis_part_obj.py`). #2342's kit project was not reused: it has no continuous operation, and its wrap golden has a stock that ends where the model ends.
- **Pictures:** three SVG files in `site/static/guide-pictures/`, drawn from the committed project, model and program by `site/tools/first_continuous_4axis_pictures.py`: the bar and the work offset, each move unrolled (X against A), and the A word line by line with the G93 lines marked. No PNG, no screenshot. The UI renderer of #1902 (PR #2078) is not merged, so there are no UI renders yet.
- **Links and corrections:** linked from Getting started, First run, "Your first 4-axis part", the Multi-axis index and "Continuous 4-axis". `continuous-4-axis.md` no longer says that no shipped post writes inverse-time feed, and the Multi-axis index no longer says that `tormach.cps` indexes A only (both untrue since #2342). `continuous-4-axis.md` has a new section "End faces and the chuck".
- `docs/decisions/1904-continuous-4axis-walkthrough.md`.

## Two findings that shape the page

1. **The page ends with an air cut and tells the reader not to cut.** Rotary Parallel finishes both end faces of the model down to the axis. On a bar held in a chuck, the chuck-side end face is inside the bar: the program feeds to Z-0.03 at X-1.3125 while the stock goes on to X-2. With a 1/2 in flute the shank check blocks the post (good); with a longer flute it posts with no warning. No setting keeps the pass off an end face. Filed as **#2343**. The page says this at the top, in "Check it" and at the end.
2. **Rotary Offset cannot be used on this machine file.** Each level that cuts takes two laps of A, and the post refuses the count past -360..360. Filed as **#2344**.

This is a partial delivery for #1904. The wrapped engraving or slot is unavailable. Neither program has a recorded PathPilot Hub run to M30. The guide describes an air cut, but no Hub run or machine run was done. Keep #1904 open for this acceptance work.

## Review fixes

Inherited parent #2342 head `b93fe06131248f91e41e90104e0d050409add852` with a merge commit. Its feed-time calculation bounds the curved part-relative trajectory from the rounded posted words. The parent includes an independent trajectory pin. This child refreshes its example program for that safety correction. The guide now explains the curved trajectory bound. Its four excerpts, stated line numbers, feed calculations and generated SVG pictures remain valid without numeric changes.

Both NC comparisons allow tightly bounded platform rounding differences. The comparisons preserve line structure and exact nonnumeric words. The independent rate checks remain. The committed program refresh is required by the inherited safety fix, rather than used to hide platform differences.

This partial delivery uses `Refs #1904`. The issue stays open for the missing Hub runs to M30 and the wrapped engraving or slot.

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/796-tormach-wrapped-a`: green (app suite `continuous_4axis_part`, 5 tests):
  - `the_continuous_4axis_part_posts_its_wrapped_program`: the committed project is byte for byte the built document; G93 on each feed that turns A with X Y Z and on no other move; A never jumps; A inside the travel
  - `the_committed_project_posts_the_committed_program`: loads with no notes, passes the machine check and the post gate
  - `each_g93_move_holds_the_a_rate`
  - `the_pass_cuts_the_chuck_side_end_face_to_the_centreline` (the fact behind "air cut only")
  - `a_short_flute_is_blocked_at_the_chuck_side_end_face`
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test continuous_4axis_part -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests`: the 13 new tests of `test_first_continuous_4axis_part.py` pass (UI labels in their sources, tables against the project, G-code excerpts as runs of the program, stated line numbers and A range, quoted refusals in the post, pictures equal to the script's output, links). 46 of 49 pass. The 3 failures are the same on the unchanged base (`test_first_4axis_part ... test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones`, `test_guide_icons` x2) and are filed as #2345.
- `zola check` in `site/`: 45 pages, no broken link.

## Not exercised

- No run in the PathPilot Hub and none on a machine. The issue's "Done means" asks for a Hub run to M30: the page lists the five things to check and asks for the result on #1904.
- The A direction on a real table, and PathPilot's own A limits (open in #2342).
- The UI steps were written from the UI sources (each bold label is held to its source by the site test); the app was not driven by hand.
- No feeds or speeds are recommended: the page says that its numbers are the example's.

Changelog: none (docs and a test-held example)

Effort: max (no escalation)

Refs #1904

body:
Stacked on #2162 (merge #2162 first)

## What changed
- Added the clean-room Mach4 milling postprocessor in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`.
- Left 3-axis programs in `G94` mode with `G20`/`G21` unit blocks, `G90 G94 G91.1 G40 G49 G17 G64` safety header, `G17`/`G18`/`G19` arcs, `G41`/`G42`/`G40` cutter compensation, `G54`..`G59` and `G54.1 P1`..`P248` work offsets, `G28`/`G53`/`G30` safe retracts, `G73`/`G81`/`G82`/`G83`/`G84`/`G85`/`G86`/`G89` canned cycles with decimal-second `P` dwells, and `G31` Macro B probing.
- Added 3+2 indexed AC trunnion support in `G94` (no `G43.4` or `G93`) using `#1962`'s trunnion schema (`A` parent of `C`, `pivot`, `offset`, `zeroOffset`, `rollover`, `signConvention`, `controller.rtcp = false`).
- Added analytical AC inverse kinematics, platter-center G54 datum transform (`work_datum = a_pivot + c_offset`), rotated cardinal arc projection, optional paired `rotaryUnclamp`/`rotaryClamp` M-codes, and safe-retract-only `C` rollover handling (`rollover_360` vs `unwrapped`).
- Added named refusals when `controller.rtcp` is `true`, when AC trunnion geometry or travel bounds are invalid or missing, or when an indexed section changes tool orientation during cutting (`"needs #1966: inverse-time feed"`).
- Registered `"Mach4"` in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and added `"Mach4"` conformance and script entries in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` and `crates/post/tests/script_mach4.rs`.
- Documented unattended choices in `docs/decisions/1968-mach4-post.md`.

## Cause
Camcraft shipped no Mach4 milling dialect, and Mach4 controllers lack native Fanuc `G43.4` RTCP while `#1966` (`G93` inverse-time feed) is not yet merged.

## Tests
- Pins added (all failed red before implementation):
  - `crates/post/tests/mach4_post.rs` (3 tests: 3-axis mm/inch dialect words and cycles, `G31` probing, `G53`/`G30` safe retracts)
  - `crates/post/tests/mach4_trunnion.rs` (3 tests: mm/inch `table_rh`/`tool_rh` 3+2 kinematics verified via `forward_part`, rollover `[0, 360)` and clamp M-code ordering, RTCP/trunnion-geometry/simultaneous refusals)
  - `crates/app/tests/mach4_builtin.rs` (2 tests: `BUILTINS` + `post_serves`, end-to-end `post_setup` on `3axis-vmc.mch`)
  - `crates/post/tests/script_mach4.rs` (`post_suite!("mach4.cps")`, 11 recorded cases)
- Mutation checks verified (each turned pinning tests red, then returned green on restore):

  - Bypassed `m.rtcp === true` check in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`: `mach4_refuses_rtcp_bad_trunnion_and_simultaneous_by_name` failed.
  - Bypassed simultaneous mid-section orientation guard in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`: `mach4_refuses_rtcp_bad_trunnion_and_simultaneous_by_name` failed.
  - Bypassed `cRollover` wrapping in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`: `mach4_rotary_rollover_unwrapped_vs_360_and_clamp_order` failed.
  - Bypassed missing `A.pivot` guard in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`: `mach4_refuses_rtcp_bad_trunnion_and_simultaneous_by_name` failed.

title: fix(ui): cache pick highlight geometry and batch stroke draws
body:
## What changed

Refresh on 2026-11-18 (merge of main `ed4a9940f`, head `56fa6694b`). The PR now keeps only caches whose key is the input itself (crates/ui/AGENTS.md, "Frame cost"):

- `crates/ui/src/frame_cache.rs`: each body's world-space vertices. The key is the facet allocation (`Weak<[Triangle]>`, compared by pointer, plus the length) and the pose bits. `world::world_verts` uses it.
- `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight.rs` (`HighlightCache`): the resolved outlines of the shown picks, the viewport hover and the Geometry-row hover. The key is the same as the key of `pick_line_memo`: the picks by value, and for each picked body its display-off flag, entity, `Arc<Features>` allocation and view pose.
- `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight_mesh.rs`: each highlight layer is one cached `egui::Shape::Mesh` in `pick_ink::paint` and in the row hover of `shell::viewport_panel`. Each of the three slots (selected, viewport hover, row hover) is a `MeshSlot` with its own build counter. A cache hit sends a clone of the `Arc<Mesh>`, not a deep copy.
- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs`: `digest_of` uses a fixed array, not a heap `Vec` for each triangle (the same hash). `patches` and `patch_rings` build the lattice one time.
- `crates/app/src/model/toolpath.rs`: `toolpath_nonempty` reads without a clone (`model.rs` only re-exports it). `operation::stamp::status_of` uses it. `toolpath_warning_count` had no caller and is removed.

The refresh removed these parts of the PR, because main has input-keyed memos for the same work, or because the key was a document counter:

- `feature/index.rs` (`*_arc` helpers): main has `model::resolve_chain`, `model::patches` and `model::patch_rings`.
- `SHARED_FEATURES_CACHE`: main has the Weak memo in `model::features_of`.
- The scene, region and toolpath-line caches: main has `frame_memo::scene_scope` and `pick_line_memo`.
- `panel_cache.rs` (six panel caches) and `History::revision_token`: keyed by a document counter.

`docs/decisions/2201-highlighter-frame-perf.md` records each choice.

## Cause

- `pick_ink::paint` and `shell::viewport_panel` sent two `Shape::LineSegment` shapes for each projected segment in each frame.
- The highlight outlines and the world vertices were built again in each frame when no input changed.

## Screenshots

The refresh is a performance change only. It adds no new visible change. The screenshots of the original change are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch:

| Selected edges | ![Before selected edges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/3441230386b638c8bfd4478b8cb22b908ff25aad/2256/before-selected-edges.png) | ![After selected edges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/3441230386b638c8bfd4478b8cb22b908ff25aad/2256/after-selected-edges.png) |

## Tests

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/highlight_perf.rs` (4 tests):
  - `three_selected_edge_pieces_draw_as_a_single_batched_highlight`
  - `selected_highlight_builds_once_at_selection_and_zero_times_across_orbit_idle_and_hover`
  - `selected_welded_patch_draws_as_batched_highlight_with_single_build`

- `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight_tests.rs` (new, counter and changed-input pins):
  - `highlight_still_frames_build_the_outline_once`
  - `highlight_rebuilds_when_the_pose_moves`
  - `highlight_rebuilds_when_the_facets_are_replaced`
  - `highlight_rebuilds_when_the_body_is_hidden_or_the_pick_changes`

- `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight_mesh_tests.rs` (new, screen-mesh cache pins, each test runs all three slots):

title: feat(ui): drag rings in Rotate mode turn the selected part
body:
The parent #1330 (drag-to-move) merged as `bd0400ebb`. This branch now has `origin/main` merged in, so the diff shows only the work of this PR.

## What changed
- The viewport bar has a new Rotate button after Move. Move and Rotate are mutually exclusive. A toggle cancels the live drag of the other mode.
- With Rotate on, the one selected part shows three rings round its bounding-box centre. Each ring is square to one shown axis. The ring radius is a constant 60 px on the screen. A press within 6 px of a ring grabs the nearest ring.
- The drag angle is the point where the cursor ray meets the ring plane, measured about the centre. The angle is unwrapped, so a drag can go past 180 degrees. During the drag the part preview turns and the bar shows `Turn about Z: +35.0°`. The world does not change during the drag.
- The release queues one `CommandKind::TurnModelBy { name, axis, angle_rad }`. The drain runs the existing `MoveModel`, so the turn is one undo step. The generated operations go stale and the stock follows the part, as for a typed turn.
- An aligned setup turns the part about the axis that the user sees (the turn goes back through the setup alignment).
- Escape cancels the turn with no history step. A turn that ends at its start angle queues nothing and writes no rotation noise (#2177).
- A bad axis, a non-finite angle or a missing part is refused by name on the status line.
- New files: `crates/ui/src/turn_drag.rs` (the drag law), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/turn_handles.rs` (the paint), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewport_bar_tests.rs` (the bar tests moved out to keep `viewport_bar.rs` near 400 lines).
- No new app command, so no new MCP tool. MCP `move_model` already sets the rotation.

## How the stale path is pinned
`body_turn::a_ring_drag_is_one_undoable_turn_that_stales_the_path_and_carries_the_stock` drags the Z ring on the seeded document. Before the drag, `camcraft_app::posting::program_ops` returns `Ok`. After the release, it returns an `Err` that contains "regenerate", so the post refuses. One undo makes the history clean again and `program_ops` returns `Ok` again. The same test checks that the stock box still holds the turned part. The app-level pin `crates/app/tests/commands_undo.rs::a_moved_part_marks_generated_ops_stale_and_undo_clears_it` already covers a pure rotation in the stale stamp.

## Refresh after #1330 (head `54ec20066`)
- Merge `3f1a72208` takes `origin/main` and keeps the two sides. Hand resolves:
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs`: the `update_hover` line of this PR (it also holds the hover during a turn), inside the `frame_cost` timing of main. The focus-loss block of main is kept.
  - `crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`: all of `CenterCache`, `pose_bits`, the cached `shown_center` and `walk_center` of main are kept. `shown_center` is `pub(crate)` so that the rings use the same cache.
- The rotate drag now obeys the move-drag rules of #1330:
  - No facet walk in a still frame. The ring centre comes from the cached `shown_center`. The paint computes the rings one time for each frame and finds the ring under the pointer from them (`turn_drag::ring_in`, `turn_handles.rs`).
  - Focus loss or pointer-gone cancels a live turn (`shell.rs`). A later release sends no command.
  - No NaN angle. A ring plane seen within 3 degrees of end-on holds the turn (`END_ON_SIN2` of #1330). A cursor within 6 px of the pivot holds the turn. A non-finite step is not added. The release still sends one undoable `TurnModelBy`.
- New tests:
  - `egui_app::tests::body_turn::focus_loss_mid_turn_cancels_and_a_later_release_sends_no_turn`
  - `turn_drag_tests::a_still_frame_walks_no_facets_and_a_turn_walks_them_again` (the counter test)
  - `turn_drag_tests::a_cursor_on_the_pivot_holds_the_turn`

## Pinning tests
- `egui_app::tests::body_turn::*` (6 tests): rings only in Rotate mode at a constant size; one undoable turn that makes the path stale and carries the stock; Escape cancels; focus loss cancels; a zero turn adds nothing; empty space still orbits.
- `turn_drag_tests::*` (8 tests): the angle under the cursor, no facet walk in a still frame, a hold at the pivot, a drag past half a turn, no command for a press off the rings or a turn in place, the centre stays in place, a turned setup, refusals by name.
- `egui_app::viewport_bar::tests::move_and_rotate_modes_never_share_the_part`.

## Readings
- Quick gate (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`) on head `54ec20066`: 17 steps, 0 failed. ui lib 1147 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored. boundary, boundary_picks, catalog_render, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, sinker_setup, tap_hand, theme_example, theme_files and waterjet_tool are green.
- Clippy `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings` on the same head: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed. No UI test was deleted or ignored.

## Not exercised
- No hand test in the live window. The screenshots come from the kittest harness render of the shipping shell with the GPU viewport, at 1280x720.
- No angle snapping (not asked for; see `docs/decisions/2047-drag-to-rotate.md`).
- `shell.rs` was already longer than 400 lines before this change; this PR adds 7 net lines to it (14 added, 7 changed).

## Screenshots
Before (Move mode of #1330 on this branch: the move balls, no rings):
![before move](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/c75bf71a4a9cb55f12442cdc2b6b5b8775178e51/pr-2047/before-move.png?raw=true)
After (Rotate mode, a Z-ring drag of +35 degrees in progress):
![after rotate](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/c75bf71a4a9cb55f12442cdc2b6b5b8775178e51/pr-2047/after-rotate.png?raw=true)

Changelog: The viewport bar has a Rotate mode: drag a ring on the selected part to turn it about an axis through its centre, as one undo step.
Effort: high

Fixes #2047

title: feat(post): 1-based script errors, loop limits, blank template and preview samples
body:
**Stacked on #468** (branch `issue/419-thread-dips`, head `d3bb673d`): both change `Script::load`. Only commit `236d40d6` is this issue's work; review that commit. Retarget/refresh after #468 merges.

## What changed (crates/post only)
- Host prelude, rotary and explanation helpers are evaluated separately from user source (`host.js` / `user.cps`), so syntax and runtime errors report the user's own 1-based line and column, with no prelude offset.
- Sandbox limits: Boa loop limit 1,000,000 iterations, recursion 64, stack 4,096, kept for every hook call; same on desktop and wasm. A post run is capped at 100,000 output lines counted across hooks; the buffer length is checked in Rust before it is reported or drained, so direct buffer writes cannot slip an oversized program through. Each limit is a named refusal.
- Host prelude moved to `js_host.rs` (re-exported from `js`, public paths unchanged) to keep `js.rs` under 400 lines (386).
- New `post::preview`: `BLANK_TEMPLATE` (original, empty hooks, emits nothing), `DEFAULT_VMC_JSON`, and `SAMPLES` - four deterministic sample streams (facing, contour, pocket, drill) built from committed goldens with setup/operation/tool/spindle/clearance records.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/2069-post-sandbox.md`. No new crate dependency.

## Pins
- `camcraft-post --test script_sandbox` (10): `syntax_errors_report_exact_user_line_and_column`, `runtime_errors_report_exact_user_line_and_column`, `endless_top_level_loop_is_refused`, `endless_hook_loop_is_refused`, `excessive_recursion_is_refused`, `excessive_stack_is_refused`, `output_limit_counts_lines_across_hooks`, `output_limit_covers_every_line_writer`, `direct_output_buffer_writes_are_refused_before_drain`, `direct_output_buffer_writes_are_refused_at_run_boundary`.
- `camcraft-post --test post_preview` (3): `blank_template_compiles_and_emits_no_lines_or_warnings`, `preview_samples_post_cleanly_and_deterministically`, `preview_samples_carry_setup_operation_tool_spindle_and_cycle_feed`.
All 13 pass on `236d40d6` (macOS, m3). The worker checked each pin with a mutation (red without the fix, green with it).

## Known inherited failures (not caused by this PR)
The quick gate shows two failures that come from #468's older base:
- `camcraft-app --test docs_troubleshooting troubleshooting_messages_still_exist_in_the_sources` - panics at `docs_troubleshooting.rs:83` ("troubleshooting page is readable: NotFound"). Fixed on main by PR #2053.
- `camcraft-app --test operations threaded_batch_matches_the_serial_loop_bit_for_bit` - panics at `operations.rs:1433`: APocket3D refuses BN-0600 (the pocket is 20 mm deep but the wider shank starts 15 mm above the tip).

Evidence: both tests were run on #468's head `d3bb673d` with this PR's changes stashed (clean tree, `git status` empty) and both failed with the same messages. This PR changes only `crates/post`; it does not touch the troubleshooting docs or the 3D pocket shank check. Neither failure is fixed here, because the fix belongs on #468's refresh from main (not pushed to #468's branch from this PR).

## Not exercised
- The UI Post Editor preview wiring (this PR provides the engine-side pieces only).
- wasm build of the limits (same Boa settings, not built here).
- Full quick gate beyond the touched post suites and the two app tests above.

Fork synced at its current main (upstream merge `09366f64e`).

Changelog: Post engine reports script errors at the user's own line and column, refuses endless loops, deep recursion and oversized output, and provides a blank post template and sample preview streams (#2069).

Fixes #2069

title: refactor(log): library and UI diagnostics become tracing events
body:
## What changed

The last slice of #163, after PR #222 (app seams: save/open/post/generate/commands) and PR #969 (app library eprintln!s and the budget-refusal events). With this, no diagnostic in the library or UI crates bypasses the one `tracing` subscriber any more.

- **Library crates** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): every non-test `eprintln!` is now a `tracing` event - refusals and fallbacks at `warn` (refused move/builder axis or C angle; multi-axis moves held vertical or radial, a rotary start on the axis, a degenerate drive curve skipped; a non-finite sim path left out or move held still; the dual iso-surface falling back to marching tetrahedra; a missing starter tool catalog), the opt-in `CAMCRAFT_PROFILE_PROJECTION` profile lines at `info`. The text of each line is unchanged.
- **Standalone bins** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): each installs a stderr subscriber with the app's filter rule (`CAMCRAFT_LOG`, else `RUST_LOG`, else `info`), so the converted library warnings still reach their terminal. Their own `println!` reports and usage errors are the CLI's answer and stay as they are.
- **UI**: the `diag` seam (#31) now emits `tracing` events natively (target `camcraft_ui`, `warn`/`info`) instead of `eprintln!`/`println!`; wasm32 still goes to the browser console. The native window (`shell_window.rs`, `shell_window/frame.rs`), GPU bring-up (`gpu_init.rs`), Cmd+Q hook (`os_quit.rs`) and the headless proof (`shell.rs`) now speak through the seam, so the law test's allow-list shrinks to the seam and test-only code (`gpu.rs`'s test module, `headless_gpu.rs`'s `device_for_test`, whose "SKIPPED - NOT a pass" line must show in a test run with no subscriber).

**Dependencies.** No new crate: `tracing` and `tracing-subscriber` are already workspace dependencies (root `Cargo.toml`, since PR #222) and in `Cargo.lock`; this PR adds `{ workspace = true }` lines for them to the five library crates and `tracing` (plus `tracing-subscriber` as a dev-dependency) to `camcraft-ui`. `Cargo.lock` gains only those dependency edges. No `camcraft-*` edge is added. Decision record: `docs/decisions/163-tracing-libs.md`.

The issue's "Done means" is now covered across the three PRs: post writes name the file and result or why not (#222), a generation budget names its limit (#969, `a_budget_refusal_names_the_limit_that_fired_at_warn`), levels come from `CAMCRAFT_LOG`/`RUST_LOG` with a quiet `info` default (#222), and the library/UI prints that bypassed the filter are gone (this PR). No event was added inside a hot loop (the geometry profile lines stay behind their env var).

## How tested

- New pinning tests:
  - `camcraft-cl` `tests/refusal_log.rs::a_refused_axis_or_angle_is_a_warning_under_the_cl_target` - a refused move axis, C angle and builder axis are each a `WARN` event under `camcraft_cl`, and a stricter filter silences them.
  - `camcraft-ui` `diag::tests::diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` - `diag_warn!`/`diag_info!` are `WARN`/`INFO` events under `camcraft_ui`, and a filter below them stays quiet.
  - `camcraft-ui` `diag::tests::shared_ui_code_prints_only_through_the_diag_seam` (existing law, allow-list tightened).
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`; Cargo changes fall back to batch scope): green on every test step in 27.9 min (geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, ui suites all ok). The clippy step fails only on the pre-existing `MIN_LABEL_PX is never used` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs:115` (upstream main, #2104, not touched here); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings -A dead_code` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The wasm32 build of the UI was not run (the diag wasm branch is unchanged).
- The real GPU window and the Windows GUI-subsystem console were not launched by hand; the converted lines are the same text through the same seam.
- Pre-existing, not from this PR: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on upstream main at 780b0a25a with `constant MIN_LABEL_PX is never used` (painted.rs:115, after PR #2095). Filed as #2104 (P2).

Branched from upstream/main 780b0a25a (the fork's own main is stale; this branch carries none of it).

Changelog: Library and UI diagnostics (refusals, multi-axis and sim fallbacks, GPU bring-up, the Cmd+Q hook) now go through the same filtered terminal log as the app's (CAMCRAFT_LOG / RUST_LOG); the standalone camcraft-cl/-geometry/-motion/-sim/-tools tools print them too.

Process change: no

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #163

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01CUsqDAAAJyAPrC37zBzbbX

## Launch-terminal screenshots

These screenshots show real launches of the native `camcraft-ui` executable in an X11 terminal.
The command uses an invalid shell name. It exercises the warning in `crates/ui/src/diag.rs` without opening a GPU window.

The after executable comes from head `33cf46fbe02052c0f67fdb1ffbf22919c3fb1bf2`.
The before executable comes from that head with only the two native diagnostic calls restored to their pre-PR form.
Those calls match `crates/ui/src/diag.rs` at baseline `780b0a25a40606dc3cc96f56ab0b2c8ecb1093e6`.
The temporary source changes were restored after capture. No executable or screenshot is in this PR branch.

Run each executable with these commands:

```sh
CAMCRAFT_LOG=info ./camcraft-ui --ui legacy
CAMCRAFT_LOG=off ./camcraft-ui --ui legacy
```

Before: the terminal prints the plain refusal for both filters.
After: the terminal shows the timestamp, `WARN` level and `camcraft_ui` target at `info`. The `off` filter suppresses the warning.
Both commands return exit code 2 in both versions.

The screenshots are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

![Before: plain diagnostic bypasses the filter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/da945c1bf2c1225c326274280fbed9ac4104ec74/2110/before.png)

![After: tracing warning obeys the filter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/da945c1bf2c1225c326274280fbed9ac4104ec74/2110/after.png)

The existing pin is `diag::tests::diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level`.
The mutation check was RED with the two old print calls. The warning assertion failed.
After restoration, the same pin was GREEN (1 passed, 0 failed).

Touched-crate clippy was RED with `-D warnings`.
It reports the existing unused `MIN_LABEL_PX` constant at `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs:115`.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` completed in 53.3 minutes.
Cargo.lock changes selected the batch tests. All nine test steps were GREEN.
The gate was RED only at clippy, for the same existing `MIN_LABEL_PX` warning.
No unrelated source change was made.

title: feat(tools): convert STEP bodies to DXF half-profiles and import/export DXF
body:
## What changed

- Added a clean-room ASCII DXF writer in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/writer.rs` (`dxf::write`, `dxf::write_bytes`, `Unit::code`) emitting `HEADER` (`$INSUNITS`), `TABLES` (`LAYER`), and `ENTITIES` (`LINE`, `ARC`, `CIRCLE`).
- Added conservative stepped-band reduction in `crates/tools/src/spun_envelope.rs` (`SpunProfile::conservative_from_bands`) merging adjacent `HolderBand`s strictly upward (`max(r)`) down to at most 31 bands (`<= 64` points) and `MIN_SEGMENT`.
- Added STEP and `ToolBody` <-> ASCII DXF half-profile conversion and DXF import in `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf.rs` and `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf_import.rs` with explicit `CENTRELINE` and `PROFILE` layers.
- Added undoable `SetToolBody` constructors (`from_dxf_bytes`, `from_dxf`, `from_step_profile`, `from_placed_profile`, `profile_dxf`) in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body_dxf.rs` over `tool_body::build_spun`.
- Registered MCP tools `import_tool_holder_dxf`, `export_tool_holder_dxf`, and `convert_tool_step_to_profile` in `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_dxf_tools.rs`.
- Added conservative-envelope and half-profile-only notices, `Import DXF…`, `Export DXF…`, `Import STEP…`, and Body tab `Convert to profile` in `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs`, `tool_profile_page.rs`, and `tool_body_page.rs`.
- Recorded architectural trade-offs in `docs/decisions/743-step-dxf-half-profile.md`.

## Cause

- Direct conversion from `HolderProfile::envelope` to `SpunProfile` failed above 31 stepped bands because `2 * 32 + 2 = 66` exceeds `MAX_POINTS` (`64`).
- CamCraft lacked an ASCII DXF writer and could not export or re-import tool holder half-profiles with an explicit centreline or enforce ISO 13399 CSYS alignment on STEP-to-profile conversion.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `camcraft-geometry::dxf_writer`: `write_and_parse_round_trip_lines_arcs_circles_layers_and_units`, `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name` (2 passed).
  - `camcraft-tools::spun::envelope::tests::thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile` (6 passed): `step_to_dxf_half_profile_envelops_every_sampled_mesh_point`, `non_revolved_step_or_fine_32_plus_band_mesh_is_conservatively_enveloped`, `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`, `dxf_half_profile_import_with_lines_and_arcs_lands_as_tool_body`, `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`, `round_trip_step_to_dxf_to_body_to_dxf_is_stable_within_tolerance`.
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile_mcp`: `mcp_holder_dxf_and_step_profile_tools_list_round_trip_undo_and_refuse` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-ui::egui_app::tests::tool_profile` (9 passed, adding `profile_tab_states_conservative_envelope_and_half_profile_rules_and_dxf_workflow` and `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`).
- Mutations (each tested red after weakening the guard and green after restore):
  - `spun_envelope::join` `max(r)` -> `min(r)`: failed `thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile`; restored green.
  - `dxf::writer` zero-length `LINE` guard bypassed: failed `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name`; restored green.
  - `tool_profile_dxf_import` centreline-crossing guard bypassed: failed `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`; restored green.
  - `step_to_spun_profile` ISO 13399 requirement replaced with `+Z` fallback: failed `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`; restored green.
  - `convert_body_draft_to_profile` clear-axis check bypassed: failed `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`; restored green.
- Gate:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` expanded to the `batch` tier (`crates/geometry/src/dxf/mod.rs` is a shared crate) and passed all 10 steps in 39.8 min with 0 failures (`geometry`, `kernel`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, `app`, `ui`, `clippy -D warnings`).

## Goldens moved

- None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Native OS file-picker modal calls (`import_profile_dxf_dialog`, `export_profile_dxf_dialog`, `import_step_profile_dialog`) delegate to desktop `rfd`; headless UI tests exercise `import_profile_dxf_from`, `export_profile_dxf_to`, `import_step_profile_from`, and `Convert to profile`.
- Release-tier `SLOW_BINARIES` (`motion:finish3d`, `motion:pivot5d`, `motion:flow`, `app:center_cut_multiaxis`) were outside the `batch` gate run.

## Overlaps

- `#2092` (stacked on `#2054`) edits different functions in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs` (`library_body`, `SetToolBody::spun`), `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs` (`sync_tool_profile_ui`, `pick_library_holder`, `run_set_tool_holder`, `editor_library_holder`), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_profile_page.rs` (lines 84-87), and `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` (lines 32, 38, 281); this PR uses `tool_body::build_spun` (no `ToolBody` struct literals) and companion modules/tail blocks; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2096` edits `envelope` and `preview_3d` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_body_page.rs`, different lines from `Convert to profile`; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2077` edits `crates/app/src/lib.rs` line 118 and `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` line 281, different lines from our additions at `lib.rs` and the tail of `all()` in `mcp/tools.rs`; whichever merges second refreshes.


## UI screenshots

Rendered with the real egui shell harness at 1600 × 1200. Before uses the exact `upstream/main` (`a277dd9d51e7b4488403b946d0a3234b71ba7504`) Profile and Body page sources. After uses this PR's page sources. The Body tab shows the same ISO 13399 STEP fixture in both captures. Native file-picker dialogs were not exercised.

Images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, commit `79de292fc`.

| Tab | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Profile | ![Profile before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/79de292fc/2100/profile-before.png) | ![Profile after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/79de292fc/2100/profile-after.png) |
| Body | ![Body before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/79de292fc/2100/body-before.png) | ![Body after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/79de292fc/2100/body-after.png) |


Changelog: Convert ISO 13399 STEP tool holders conservatively into half-profile ASCII DXFs, add clean-room ASCII DXF writer/importer, and support DXF/STEP profile workflows across UI and MCP (#743).

Fixes #743
