title: feat(tools)!: a tool's library holder is a reference to the entry
body:
Stacked on #2054 (branch `mkinney:issue/2018-weldon-per-taper`, with `main` merged in for #2029). Merge #2054 first; this diff then shows only the #2016 commits. Fork synced from upstream `main` at c86d6db35.

## What changed

A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a reference to the entry, not a drawn copy of its outline.

- `camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (new, `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs`), carried on `ToolBody::library`.
- `tool_body::build_library` is the one place a reference becomes a shape. `SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool` (stated and machine-default holder), the project loader and the `.camtools` reader call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before. The #828 floor for a machine-default holder is unchanged.
- Files: the tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true` when assumed) is written in place of `body`. Project v62 (the unreleased step the issue names); a `.camtools` file says version 2 when a tool names a library holder.
- Migration: an older file is not rewritten. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a custom drawn profile with the same outline, and a `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder stays the tool's own numbers.
- Refusals by tool name: an entry the library does not hold, a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon"), lengths the entry cannot take, a holder that reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, `holder` beside `body`. No other holder is put in its place.
- MCP: `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference; the reply and `get_job` show it as `holder.library`. `add_tool` refuses a `holder` reference inside `definition`; `edit_tool` refuses a `holder` patch. Skill rows updated.
- UI: with a referenced holder the tool settings show the holder diameter and length the laws read as text, not as two fields. The Profile tab names the entry and the picker shows it. The unchanged outline applied again keeps the reference; one edited point makes the holder a custom profile (one undo step).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2016-holder-reference.md`.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on the final head (tools, app and ui suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. macOS (m5).

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/holder_reference.rs`
  - `every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy`: for every library entry, at the default and at other lengths, picked and assumed: the judged tool, envelope, band stack, stamp term and facets equal those of the drawn copy an older build stored, also after a save and load.
  - `an_older_project_loads_as_custom_holders_with_the_same_collision_result`: a v61 project with a drawn copy and a plain holder cylinder loads with the same reads, operation status and warnings (the BT30 flange strikes the fixture wall, hit for hit).
  - `an_older_tool_library_loads_as_custom_holders_and_a_new_one_round_trips_the_reference`
  - `an_unknown_entry_refuses_the_file_by_name_and_never_lands_another_holder` (project and `.camtools`)
  - `a_library_holder_is_the_reference_in_the_document_and_the_file`
  - `the_unchanged_outline_keeps_the_reference_and_an_edited_point_makes_it_custom`
  - `mcp_set_tool_holder_writes_the_reference`
- `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs` unit tests.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_holder_reference.rs`: `a_library_holder_sizes_the_holder_fields_until_its_outline_is_edited`, `the_profile_tab_names_the_entry_and_the_picker_shows_it`.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux. The release tier and the pixel-snapshot lanes (no snapshot PNG changed).
- No real v0.21.0 file was read: the older file in the tests is this build's file rewritten to the older form (`body` with the drawn copy, version 61 / 1).
- The app was not driven by hand.

## Notes for the reviewer

- A build of main between #1453 and this change reads v62 and would drop the `holder` key (development builds only; v0.21.0 refuses v62).
- A corrected library entry now reaches every project that names it. A copy kept the old numbers.
- The tool record's `holder_d`/`holder_len` are not overwritten by the entry (they are what the tool goes back to when the holder is cleared, and writing them would move the stamp). The settings show the entry's numbers.

Changelog: A tool's library holder is stored as a reference to the library entry (name, gauge length, projection) in the project and tool library files, not as a drawn copy; the tool settings show the entry's holder size. Breaking: v0.21.0 and older refuse a file that names a library holder.

Effort: max (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: a project or tool library saved with a library holder states it as a reference (project v62, `.camtools` version 2); v0.21.0 and older refuse such a file.

Process change: yes

Fixes #2016

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01CUsqDAAAJyAPrC37zBzbbX

## UI screenshots

These images show the seeded `EM-0600-4FL` tool with the `BT30 ER20` holder.
The gauge length is 60 mm. The projection is 55 mm.

The egui test harness drives the production shell and renders these PNGs with the GPU renderer.
The before captures use the four UI and profile-state source files from `e661ece1`.
The backend stays at `822c4c9a` to supply the same holder geometry in both captures.
The after captures use the current head, `822c4c9a`.

### Holder size controls

Before: the holder diameter and length are editable fields.

![Holder size controls before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ba10296eb7199e2b37254900e26f188302e5a1c8/2092/holder-controls-before.png)

After: the controls show the library holder diameter and length, with the entry name.

![Holder size controls after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ba10296eb7199e2b37254900e26f188302e5a1c8/2092/holder-controls-after.png)

### Profile tab

Before: the tab identifies a drawn profile. The library picker has no selection.

![Holder Profile tab before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ba10296eb7199e2b37254900e26f188302e5a1c8/2092/holder-profile-before.png)

After: the tab names the library holder. The picker shows `BT30 ER20`, the gauge length, and the projection.

![Holder Profile tab after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ba10296eb7199e2b37254900e26f188302e5a1c8/2092/holder-profile-after.png)

- Added the `set_stock_material { "material": string | null }` row to Section 4 of `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`.

body:
## What changed

- Added off-screen `ShellUi` + `View3D` guide capture harness in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_images.rs`.
- Added three clean-room demo project builders in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_projects.rs` and committed `examples/guide-workholding.camproj`, `examples/guide-3d.camproj`, and `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`.
- Added `cargo xtask docs-images [--check]` in `xtask/src/docs_images.rs` and wired it into `xtask/src/main.rs`.
- Rendered and committed 13 optimised 1200x760 guide PNGs in `site/static/images/guide/` (`setup-overview.png`, `workholding-vise-toolpath.png`, `op-2d-pocket-params.png`, `op-2d-{stepover,entry,lead}-{before,after}.png`, `op-3d-pocket-roughing.png`, `op-3d-finish-parallel.png`, `op-multiaxis-swarf.png`, `op-indexed-3plus2.png`).
- Embedded all 13 images with descriptive alt text across Setups, Workholding, 2D, 3D, Multi-axis, and Indexed guide pages.
- Added `.guide-content img` and `.guide-pair` layout rules in `site/static/style.css`.
- Added `site/tests/test_guide_images.py`, `xtask/tests/docs_images.rs`, and `docs/decisions/1902-docs-guide-images.md`.

## Cause

The User Guide relied solely on SVG path diagrams without screenshots of CamCraft's UI, setup tree, workholding fixtures, 3D views, or parameter before/after pairs.

## Tests

title: feat(ui): report door with prefilled GitHub issue and clipboard screenshot
body:
## What changed

The status strip gains a Report door next to the Debug info door (#1696).
It opens a small window:

- A short title field.
- Two buttons, "Report a bug" and "Request a feature". Each opens the
  browser on a prefilled GitHub new-issue URL: the title, the body and the
  `bug` / `enhancement` label are already typed.
- A "Copy screenshot" button. It asks the shell for a picture of the whole
  application window: egui's `ViewportCommand::Screenshot`, answered by the
  native shell's capture module (`shell_window/capture.rs`, a second render
  pass of the same frame into a private texture). The picture goes to the
  clipboard. The user pastes it into the issue description and GitHub
  uploads it.

The body embeds the Debug info report (#157), so both paths carry the same
fields from one source. When no answer arrives, the copy names that in
words, in the status line.

Provenance: the mechanism is egui's public capture contract. The maintainer
pointed at SolidCraft's report dialog for the shape only; their code was
not read and their look is not used.

The repository also gains `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/blank-issue.md` and
`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` (GitHub reads `blank_issues_enabled`
only from that path). The new glyph `act-report.png` is the Tabler Icons
(MIT) `banner` glyph; its SVG master `assets/ui/svg/act-report.svg` sits
with our masters and `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` names Tabler as its source.

## How tested

- `report_tests.rs` (new, kittest): URL encoding; the prefilled URL shape;
  the body content; the door open and a kind button filing the URL; the
  typed title in the URL; a kind button asking the shell for the whole
  window; the answer copying the picture and saying the word; the copy
  after the window is closed; an answer for another token left alone; no
  answer copying nothing. 10 tests.
- `structural.rs`: the door sits on the status strip; no floating window is
  open by default (pin kept).
- `op_icon_table.rs`: the `Report` glyph is SVG-mastered and unique.
- `cargo xtask icons --check`: 0 breaches.
- The maintainer GUI-tested the debug build on 2026-11-17 and said it looks
  good: door, window, browser open with the prefilled issue, and the
  whole-window picture on the clipboard.
- Quick gate on the final head is named in the ready comment below.

## Not exercised here

- Clipboard paste into GitHub in an automated test: the tests assert the
  clipboard write, not GitHub. The maintainer's GUI test covered the paste
  path.

Note for the reviewer: this PR touches `.github/`, so `pr-test.yml` refuses
it and the review builds locally (read, not built: the yellow
`needs-maintainer` path).

Branch merges origin/main at 16658f67b.

Changelog: The status strip gained a Report door: it opens a prefilled GitHub issue and copies a whole-window screenshot to the clipboard (#1696, PR #1798)

title: feat(ui): drag a part along an axis with move handles (#1198 b)
body:
#1198 slice (b): move handles with drag-to-move. Slice (a), the bottom bar, merged in #1203. Slice (c), the rotate handles, is #2047. Slice (d), snapping and typed values, stays on #1198.

**GUI hand check needed.** The kittest harness and headless state tests test the handles, the drag and the readout. The offscreen screenshots below come from the same harness. Nobody has examined them on a real screen with real mouse input.

## What changed
- **Move mode in the bottom bar.** A new bar button (a four-armed cross, after Pick through) turns `State::move_handles` on and off. It is off by default. It is view state like Pick through, and it queues no command.
- **Handles** (`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`, painted by `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`). With Move on and exactly one shown part selected, three arms in the axis colours start at the bounding-box centre of the part. Each arm ends in a ball. The arms stay 70 px long on screen at all zoom levels. The ball under the pointer is drawn larger.
- **Drag.** A press on a ball takes the press before orbit and pick. A press on empty space still orbits. When a nav tool of the bar (Orbit, Pan, Zoom) is latched, that tool owns the press. While the button is down, the preview moves the body along the axis (`world.rs` draws it with an offset) and never writes the world. The signed distance shows above the bar. The distance is the point where the cursor ray is nearest to the axis line, so the part stays under the cursor in perspective and in ortho.
- **One command per drag.** The release queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy { name, delta }`. The drain (`crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs`) runs it as the `MoveModel::new` of the Model page, with the rotation copied bit for bit. Thus a drag is one undo step, with the same staleness, the same following stock and the same fixture-clash warning as a typed move. There is no new placement path.
- **No history step for:** Escape during a drag (the key is consumed), a drag that ends at its start point, and Move turned off.
- **Turned setups.** When the active setup holds the part turned (#326), the drag occurs in the frame of that setup. The shown delta is rotated back into the document frame, so the part moves along the axis that the user sees.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/1198-drag-to-move.md`: only parts are dragged in this slice, Move mode is off by default, and the preview moves the body only.

## MCP
No new app command, thus no new MCP tool. `MoveModelBy` is a UI queue verb over the existing `MoveModel`. The MCP `move_model` tool (`crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs`) already places a part through `MoveModel`. An agent can make each move that a drag makes.

## Screenshots (offscreen, kittest harness with the headless GPU viewport)
The "before" is Move off on this branch: on `main` the bar has no Move button, and all else is the same.

| X ball dragged (preview, readout above the bar) | After the release (one `MoveModel`) |

| ![Dragging](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/screenshots/pr-1330/3-dragging.png?raw=true) | ![Released](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/screenshots/pr-1330/4-released.png?raw=true) |

## Refresh for merge (2026-11-18)
- Old head: `58df4b729`. New head: `553f6c2e6` (merge of `origin/main` at `b629dc7e8`). No rebase, no force-push.
- Two conflicts, resolved by hand. Both sides are kept:
  - `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: the `move_by` module line of this PR and the `fixture_turn_ui` lines of main.
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs`: main wraps `update_hover` in `frame_cost::time`. This PR adds `|| state.body_drag.is_some()` to the press argument. The merged line has the two changes.

## How tested (on head `3d394d6f4`, debug, `-j 6`, `--test-threads=6`)

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
The stack parents #517 (#417) and #518 (#418) are merged. The diff now holds only the #419 work.

## Merge-time refresh (maintainer's session, head 39632f647)
The maintainer's session took this PR over for a merge-time refresh. It merged `origin/main` (62e1d36a6) into the branch. It did not rebase or force-push.

Hand-resolved hunks (keep both sides):
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, `threadHalfTurn`: the PR's dip chain is kept. Main changed the lead word from `fr()` to `fl()` (#902: an inch lead has six decimals). Both G32 blocks of the chain (the plain block and the dip block `G32 X Z F`) now use `fl()`. The three refusals of the chain (no open chain, steeper than 45 degrees, deeper than the pass) are kept.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, manifest: `continuousThreading = true` with its citation, and main's `workOffsetIndex`, `workOffsetMax`, `explainWords`, `explainTool`, `programUnits`, `explains`, `commentMax`, `explainBlockMax`.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, G76 header comment: the PR's chip-break dips clause and main's `g76Allowance` paragraph (#517). `g76Why` keeps the two refusals: `RepeatEachDepth` (#518) and `ChipBreakDips`.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: main's manifest list with `continuousThreading` added ("the last nine").
- `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs`: the `ChipBreakDips` refusal and main's `MillSpindle` reverse refusal (#988).
- `crates/post/src/post/js.rs`: the `continuous_threading` and `mill_spindle_reverse` fields.

No refusal of #517, #518 or main is lost. The Tormach lathe post does not declare `continuousThreading`, so the engine refuses dips on it by name. Its G76 `RepeatEachDepth` refusal (#518) is unchanged. `git diff origin/main --stat` lists only the 26 files of this PR.

Readings after the refresh (`cargo test -j 6 -p <crate> --test <binary>`, one binary at a time):
- camcraft-motion: `turning_thread_dips` 9/9, `turning_thread_cycle` 3/3, `turning_thread_infeed` 10/10, lib 366 passed (5 ignored).
- camcraft-post: `inverted_post` 16/16, `recorded_streams` 12/12, lib 54/54.
- camcraft-cl: lib 41/41.
- camcraft-app: `lathe_post_thread_dips` 6/6 (golden `thread_g32_dips.nc` unchanged), `lathe_post_g76` 8/8, `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 7/7, `lathe_post_tormach_thread` 8/8, `lathe_post_css` 10/10, `turning_thread` 10/10, `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5, `lathe_thread_travel` 2/2, `conformance` 7/7, `coarse_laws` 6/6, `lathe_field_tools` 2/2, `project_roundtrip` 73/73.
- camcraft-ui: lib filter `thread` 6/6.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised by the refresh: an inch program with dips (the `fl()` lead word under G20 has no golden), and a run on a controller or a simulator.

MCP: the dips ride the generic `edit_operation` tool through the project params JSON (`ThreadInfeedDto.dips`). No new MCP tool is necessary.

Screenshots: before and after screenshots on the refreshed head are in the section "Screenshots (Passes tab)" below.

Note: `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs` (600 lines) and `js.rs` (529 lines) were already more than 400 lines on main. This PR adds 4 and 17 lines to them.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`

## How tested
- **New motion `turning_thread_dips`** (8 tests):
  - dips off lay the plain path bit for bit;
  - a dip is never deeper than its pass;
  - the phase is unchanged across the chain;
  - placement and slope rules hold;
  - a repeated depth cuts whole;
  - the verdict is silent on laid dips;
  - the verdict convicts each broken law (first/last lead, finishing pass, deeper, phase shift, steep). Temporarily disabling the laws made this test fail.
  - refusals by name.
- **New app `lathe_post_thread_dips`** (6 tests):
  - the golden `thread_g32_dips.nc`;
  - the posted chain keeps the plain thread's Z words and lead;
  - G76 refuses;
  - a post without `continuousThreading` refuses;
